nodes.description:
**Practice:** Before committing to a grand opening, validate that the food quality and overall experience are strong enough that word-of-mouth alone can sustain the location to full capacity within six months.

**Practice:** Reframe the restaurant marketing budget question for finance partners: instead of asking how much to spend on ads, ask how much premium is being paid across systems, service, and ingredients to increase word-of-mouth virality.

_from why_your_restaurant_marketing_doesn_t_matter_u99G6KwRWQ0.txt_

**Practice:** Send candidates the sales script before any interview and require a 60-second video of them reciting it as the first screening gate.

nodes.description:
**Practice:** Run group coaching calls (not individual interviews) for sales rep candidates; drill the script live, give feedback, and observe whether candidates are coachable.

nodes.label: Require script memorization and verbatim delivery as a non-negotiable condition …
nodes.description:
**Practice:** Require script memorization and verbatim delivery as a non-negotiable condition of employment for all reps; treat deviation as a fireable offense.

nodes.plugin: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence
nodes.description:
**Practice:** Conduct daily sales training sessions to keep all reps delivering the script correctly and consistently.

_from why_your_sales_team_tanks_after_every_big_month_IVNuDhV1uw4.txt_
nodes.parent_id: concept:Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence
nodes.topic: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

**Practice:** Before attempting a cultural gut-and-rebuild, implement the full sales ops checklist (script enforcement, daily training, daily huddles, career goal conversations); only escalate to mass termination if the checklist fails due to entrenched cultural resistance.

nodes.description:
**Practice:** Hold the sales manager accountable as the primary lever for team performance — if the team has persistent culture problems, diagnose whether the manager is reinforcing the right behaviors before making rep-level changes.

nodes.parent_id: concept:Leadership Sets Culture; Culture Determines Acceptable Effort
nodes.topic: Leadership Sets Culture; Culture Determines Acceptable Effort

nodes.description:
**Practice:** Whatever reason you need to give yourself to increase the likelihood that you take the required actions is sufficient justification for that reason, regardless of how the reason sounds or whether it is socially acceptable (e.g., jealousy, rage).

_from you_don_t_have_to_feel_good_enough_to_win_HwTWXXoVm-8.txt_

nodes.label: Define your input-output equation before increasing volume: identify the specifi…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** Define your input-output equation before increasing volume: identify the specific action that moves you toward your goal, then multiply that action by 10x. If you can reach 10x, figure out how to reach 100x.

_from you_don_t_need_2x_more_effort_you_need_10x_Qq-iYKtyF0U.txt_

nodes.label: Recognize that the control behaviors that made you successful as a self-employed…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** Recognize that the control behaviors that made you successful as a self-employed person must be actively unlearned as you scale; treat relinquishing each business function (delivery, admin, sales, marketing, management, leadership, financing) as a sequential milestone rather than a loss.

_from you_don_t_need_2x_more_effort_you_need_10x_Qq-iYKtyF0U.txt_

nodes.label: When something bad happens, recover your emotional and behavioral baseline befor…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** When something bad happens, recover your emotional and behavioral baseline before talking to anyone else in your life — contain the setback before it spreads.

nodes.label: Use whatever motivational fuel you currently have — shame, deprivation, anger, a…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** Use whatever motivational fuel you currently have — shame, deprivation, anger, aspiration — rather than waiting for a narratively 'acceptable' source of motivation. The rule is: use what you have.

_from you_ll_find_this_video_when_you_need_it_1vHTG2WEoYc.txt_

nodes.label: Treat a bad day the same as any other day in terms of how you behave toward your…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** Treat a bad day the same as any other day in terms of how you behave toward your spouse, children, and colleagues. A bad day is not moral permission to misbehave.

_from you_ll_find_this_video_when_you_need_it_1vHTG2WEoYc.txt_

nodes.description:
**Practice:** When one bad thing happens, actively prevent it from touching other life domains (health, marriage, parenting, business) by isolating it and not using it as justification for abandoning self-control in those other areas.

_from you_ll_find_this_video_when_you_need_it_1vHTG2WEoYc.txt_

nodes.label: When scaling paid ads, sequence your moves: first make more creative, then incre…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** When scaling paid ads, sequence your moves: first make more creative, then increase budget, then expand to new platforms. Do not increase budget before building creative volume.

**Practice:** Before a major launch, bank a large creative library (e.g., 2,000+ ads) by hiring additional editors well in advance; do not rely on a small editorial team to generate launch-scale creative output in real time.

_from you_need_to_advertise_more_lBNpcvKvf38.txt_

nodes.label: When assessing the quality of your work, ask whether there is anything you can s…

**Practice:** When assessing the quality of your work, ask whether there is anything you can still remove, add, or clarify; only declare it done when the answer to all three is no.

_from you_need_to_work_100x_harder_otJE7ij924s.txt_

nodes.label: Track your effort investment in a domain by counting in hundreds of hours rather…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** Track your effort investment in a domain by counting in hundreds of hours rather than hours, to force engagement with the actual depth of mastery required.

_from you_need_to_work_100x_harder_otJE7ij924s.txt_

nodes.label: When your work is submitted, ask: if I had two more weeks, would I approach this…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** When your work is submitted, ask: if I had two more weeks, would I approach this differently? If the answer is yes, you have not yet reached your attainable quality ceiling.

_from you_need_to_work_100x_harder_otJE7ij924s.txt_

nodes.label: When you do not feel good about continuing, keep going anyway; the emotional sta…
nodes.description:
**Practice:** When you do not feel good about continuing, keep going anyway; the emotional state is temporary and will pass, while the work you complete in the meantime remains.

_from you_re_not_a_victim_of_your_circumstances_keep_going_LOSLhlb5GKM.txt_

nodes.label: When assessing the value of a period of apparent failure, audit what skills and …
nodes.description:
**Practice:** When assessing the value of a period of apparent failure, audit what skills and experiences you developed, not only what financial or external outcomes you produced.

nodes.label: Before attributing your uncompleted goals to circumstances (children, location, …

nodes.label: Four Types of Trust
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Types of Trust** — A 2x2 framework mapping trust by (1) who bears the risk and (2) who does the punishing, yielding four trust types: self-risk-other-punishes, other-risk-self-punishes, self-risk-environment-punishes, other-risk-environment-punishes.

nodes.label: Core Four Advertising Methods
nodes.description: **Framework: Core Four Advertising Methods** — The only four ways a person can let others know about what they sell, derived from combining two audience types (warm/cold) with two communication modes (one-to-one/one-to-many): warm outreach, posting free content, cold outreach, and paid ads.

nodes.label: Lead Getter Hierarchy
nodes.description: **Framework: Lead Getter Hierarchy** — Four types of external parties who advertise on your behalf in ascending order of leverage: customers (referrals), employees, agencies, and affiliates; each multiplies lead flow beyond what a single founder can generate.

nodes.label: More Better New
nodes.description: **Framework: More Better New** — A three-stage framework for scaling any advertising channel: first maximize volume (more), then improve conversion rates at the biggest drop-off constraint (better), then expand to new placements, platforms, or core four activities (new).

nodes.label: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate
nodes.description: **Framework: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate** — A three-step employee training model: document every step of the task as a checklist while performing it, demonstrate the checklist step-by-step in front of the trainee, then have the trainee duplicate the process while being observed.

nodes.label: Whisper-Tease-Shout Launch Method
nodes.description: **Framework: Whisper-Tease-Shout Launch Method** — A three-phase product and affiliate launch sequence: whisper (create curiosity months out with behind-the-scenes hints), tease (reveal value elements and date weeks out), shout (issue specific CTAs with urgency and scarcity in the final days).

nodes.label: What-Who-When Ad Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: What-Who-When Ad Framework** — An advertising copywriting structure that combines the eight value elements (dream outcome, perceived likelihood, time delay, effort) with multiple stakeholder perspectives (prospect, spouse, colleagues, rivals) and three time horizons (past, present, future) to generate compelling ad angles.

nodes.label: Seven-Step Lead Magnet Creation
nodes.description: **Framework: Seven-Step Lead Magnet Creation** — A sequential process for building a high-converting lead magnet: identify the narrow problem and right avatar, select solution type (reveal problem / sample / one step of multi-step), choose delivery mechanism (software / information / service / physical product), test naming, maximize ease of consumption, maximize quality, and add a clear CTA.

nodes.label: Generate Flow, Monetize Flow, Add Friction
nodes.description: **Framework: Generate Flow, Monetize Flow, Add Friction** — A three-stage acquisition sequencing model: start with the highest-volume (free or deeply discounted) front end to generate lead flow, monetize that flow, then progressively add friction to raise lead quality over time.

nodes.label: Four Ways to Display Discounts
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Ways to Display Discounts** — A framework for structuring discount offers across four display formats (dollar off, percentage off, buy-X-get-Y, limited-time unit price) so businesses can test which representation drives the highest response rate for a given price point.

nodes.label: Five Friction Levers
nodes.description: **Framework: Five Friction Levers** — Five controllable mechanisms for raising free-offer lead quality while reducing volume: increased qualifications, information requirements and question types, number of steps, forced consumption of sales material, and advertisement length.

nodes.label: Two-Step Sale
nodes.description: **Framework: Two-Step Sale** — A sales architecture that splits the close into two appointments: a low-cost or discounted first transaction that captures card-on-file and builds trust, followed by a second appointment where the core high-ticket offer is sold as an upsell.

nodes.label: Four Offer Types Money Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Offer Types Money Model** — A sequenced offer stack combining Attraction Offers (strangers to customers), Upsell Offers (spend more), Downsell Offers (yes when they would say no), and Continuity Offers (keep buying) to maximize 30-day profit and recurring revenue.

nodes.label: Payment Plan Downsell Process
nodes.description: **Framework: Payment Plan Downsell Process** — A seven-step funnel shifting from full prepayment to free trial: (1) reward prepay with discount, (2) 3rd-party financing/credit card/layaway, (3) half now half later, (4) desire check 1-10 scale, (5) three-payment split, (6) evenly spread payments, (7) free trial with card.

nodes.label: Menu Upsell Four-Tactic Process
nodes.description: **Framework: Menu Upsell Four-Tactic Process** — A structured upsell sequence combining Unselling (cross out what they don't need), Prescription Upselling (tell them exactly what they do need), A/B Upselling (ask preference between two options), and Card On File (make payment frictionless).

nodes.label: Anchor Upsell Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Anchor Upsell Framework** — A five-step premium-first pricing process: present anchor (5-10x premium), get the gasp, come to the rescue by asking what makes the premium matter to them, present core offer, ask how they want to pay.

nodes.label: Win Your Money Back Offer
nodes.description: **Framework: Win Your Money Back Offer** — An attraction offer where customers pay upfront and earn their money back as cash or store credit if they meet defined results, actions, or both criteria; the real profit comes from the upsell made to successful customers.

nodes.label: Grand Slam Offer
nodes.description: **Framework: Grand Slam Offer** — An offer combining an attractive promotion, unmatchable value proposition, premium price, and unbeatable guarantee with a money model that lets you get paid to acquire customers, creating a category of one with no direct price comparison.

nodes.label: The Value Equation
nodes.description: **Framework: The Value Equation** — A four-variable formula for perceived value: (Dream Outcome x Perceived Likelihood of Achievement) divided by (Time Delay x Effort & Sacrifice). Maximizing the numerators and minimizing the denominators increases willingness to pay.

nodes.label: M-A-G-I-C Naming Formula
nodes.description: **Framework: M-A-G-I-C Naming Formula** — A five-component offer naming framework: Magnetic reason why + Avatar announcement + Goal statement + Interval (time duration) + Container word (bundle descriptor). Applies 3-5 components to create a name that attracts the target avatar and signals unique value.

nodes.label: Sales-to-Fulfillment Continuum
nodes.description: **Framework: Sales-to-Fulfillment Continuum** — A trade-off axis between ease of selling (high fulfillment burden) and ease of fulfillment (harder to sell); the optimal sweet spot is a highly sellable offer that is also operationally manageable. Start by over-delivering, then systematize.

nodes.label: Virtuous Cycle of Price
nodes.description: **Framework: Virtuous Cycle of Price** — A causal loop in which premium pricing increases client emotional investment, perceived value, and results, attracting better clients and generating margin to reinvest in service quality, which sustains premium pricing. The inverse vicious cycle applies when prices are cut.

nodes.label: Ad Assembly Line Process
nodes.description: **Framework: Ad Assembly Line Process** — Decompose ad creation into three interchangeable components (hook, meat, CTA) produced in bulk separately, then assembled combinatorially to generate 150-750 unique ads per week from a single recording session.

nodes.label: Five Ad Meat Formats
nodes.description: **Framework: Five Ad Meat Formats** — Five proven content formats for the body of an ad: Demonstration, Testimonial, Education, Story, and Faceless; these formats work across all industries and can be mixed and matched.

nodes.label: Audience Awareness Ladder (adapted from Eugene Schwartz)
nodes.description: **Framework: Audience Awareness Ladder (adapted from Eugene Schwartz)** — A five-level model mapping ad hook style to audience knowledge state: Most Aware (offer-driven), Product-Aware (proof-driven), Solution-Aware (promise-driven), Problem-Aware (pain-driven), Completely Unaware (curiosity-driven).

nodes.label: Four Pillars of Lead Nurture
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Pillars of Lead Nurture** — A four-part framework (Availability, Speed, Personalization, Volume) derived from analysis of 4,000+ daily appointments in ALAN software that identifies the primary drivers of show rates for scheduled sales appointments.

nodes.label: BAMFAM
nodes.description: **Framework: BAMFAM** — Book-A-Meeting-From-A-Meeting: always schedule the next appointment during the current appointment rather than following up later, to prevent leads from going cold between calls.

nodes.label: Lead Nurture Throughput Math
nodes.description: **Framework: Lead Nurture Throughput Math** — Three-metric model: Schedule Rate (engaged leads who schedule) x Show Rate (scheduled leads who show) = Throughput (total engaged leads who show). Optimizing any variable compounds the others.

nodes.label: Suffering as Fixed Cost
nodes.plugin: All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice
nodes.description: **Framework: Suffering as Fixed Cost** — Suffering is an invariant cost incurred on any life path; the variable is the return you choose to demand for that suffering.
nodes.parent_id: concept:All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice
nodes.topic: All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice

nodes.label: Perceived Lack of Options Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Perceived Lack of Options Model** — Sadness is operationally defined as a perceived lack of options; options are expanded not by changing circumstances but by changing the trades one is willing to make.

nodes.label: Three-Variable Lead Viability Math
nodes.description: **Framework: Three-Variable Lead Viability Math** — A channel's economic viability is determined by exactly three numbers: cost per lead, close rate (% of leads converted), and average deal size. Their product determines CAC and whether the channel is profitable.

nodes.label: Funnel Friction Stacking
nodes.description: **Framework: Funnel Friction Stacking** — When a funnel generates too many unqualified leads, add qualification gates in sequence — first in ad copy, then in opt-in fields (scored questions), then by gating the scheduler behind a score threshold — until the unqualified volume is filtered out.

nodes.label: Single-Behavior Leverage Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Single-Behavior Leverage Framework** — Identify one behavior or skill with the highest number of positive downstream impacts; high leverage means one input produces many large outcomes.

nodes.label: Half-Step Frame Repackaging
nodes.description: **Framework: Half-Step Frame Repackaging** — Keep existing content substance (hooks, stories, topics) unchanged but shift the narrative frame from end-user perspective to practitioner-facing case-study perspective, changing the audience attracted without rebuilding the content library.

nodes.label: Four-Component Mental Toughness Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Four-Component Mental Toughness Model** — Mental toughness has four measurable variables: (1) threshold — how much adversity before behavior changes; (2) magnitude — how much behavior changes once it does; (3) resilience — how fast behavior returns to baseline; (4) adaptation — whether the rebound lands above, at, or below the original baseline.

nodes.label: Five Levels of Friendship
nodes.description: **Framework: Five Levels of Friendship** — A hierarchy for evaluating friendship depth: Level 1 = talk about the past; Level 2 = talk about other people; Level 3 = talk about ideas; Level 4 = can do things together; Level 5 = can make, lose, and spend money together.

nodes.label: Two-Question Decision Razor
nodes.description: **Framework: Two-Question Decision Razor** — Before acting on an impulse, ask (1) what do I want to have happen? and (2) what action increases the odds of that happening? The initial gut reaction is usually antithetical to both answers.

nodes.label: More, Better, New Scaling Hierarchy
nodes.description: **Framework: More, Better, New Scaling Hierarchy** — Three categories of business moves in descending risk-adjusted return order: More (repeat what works), Better (small variation on what works), New (wholly different action). New is highest resource cost and lowest probability of success; most businesses should limit themselves to one New per year.

nodes.label: Anchor Upsell with Downsell Fallback
nodes.description: **Framework: Anchor Upsell with Downsell Fallback** — Present the premium tier (e.g., $100K) as the primary offer and sell it fully before offering a stripped-down version at a lower price; the buyer who declines the premium has already mentally justified its value, making the downsell feel like a bargain.

nodes.label: Qualified Questionnaire Funnel
nodes.description: **Framework: Qualified Questionnaire Funnel** — Replace a generic request-for-quote form with a multi-question quiz that captures budget and fit signals; route qualified leads directly to a booking calendar while disqualified leads receive a PDF or no-book outcome.

nodes.label: Multi-Stage Business Scaling Roadmap
nodes.description: **Framework: Multi-Stage Business Scaling Roadmap** — A 10-stage progression across 8 business functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, human resources, finance) mapped from zero to $100M+, derived from reviewing all Acquisition.com portfolio companies and where they got stuck.

nodes.label: Core Four Acquisition Channels
nodes.description: **Framework: Core Four Acquisition Channels** — Four mutually exclusive methods for getting customers: paid ads, organic content, cold outreach, and affiliate/partner referral. Every business should map which of the four it currently uses before deciding what to add.

nodes.label: Six Pillars of Self-Work
nodes.description: **Framework: Six Pillars of Self-Work** — Alex Hormozi's summary of personal development reduced to six interdependent principles: thoughts are not inherently true, feelings do not mandate action, events have no inherent good or bad nature, ignorance is the primary enemy, changing surroundings changes behavior, and actions (not past) define identity.

nodes.label: Yeti Can Vacuum Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Yeti Can Vacuum Model** — A mental model for separating internal emotional state from behavioral output, analogous to a double-walled vacuum insulated can: feelings are on one side, actions on the other, with deliberate space (time) as the insulating layer between them.

nodes.label: Value Equation for Affiliate Activation
nodes.description: **Framework: Value Equation for Affiliate Activation** — Three levers for getting affiliates to act: reduce risk (testimonials, ongoing payments), increase speed (urgency window), and increase ease (pre-built emails, landing pages, CRM setup).

nodes.label: System 1 / System 2 Decision Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: System 1 / System 2 Decision Framework** — Daniel Kahneman's distinction between fast, automatic, unconscious mental processes (System 1) and slow, deliberative, conscious processes (System 2); Sutherland treats advertising and politics as System 1 businesses.

nodes.label: Choice Architecture
nodes.description: **Framework: Choice Architecture** — Changing the structural framing of a decision — order of options, default presentation, group vs. individual selection — to alter outcomes without changing underlying preferences or using coercion.

nodes.label: Costly Signalling Theory
nodes.description: **Framework: Costly Signalling Theory** — Biological concept in which a signal derives credibility precisely from its expense or difficulty; in marketing, costly advertising is a commitment device that signals the brand has a reputation at stake.

nodes.label: Depth-Plus-Breadth Skill Architecture
nodes.description: **Framework: Depth-Plus-Breadth Skill Architecture** — A career model requiring deep mastery in one discipline combined with breadth across related fields; depth alone is insufficient for high-value roles in fast-changing industries.

nodes.label: VSL Pre-Frame Close System
nodes.description: **Framework: VSL Pre-Frame Close System** — A three-part cold-outbound close architecture: (1) VSL that pre-frames the prospect before the call, (2) scripted qualification and pre-frame on the call, (3) training cadence ensuring reps follow the process — designed to move close rates from 6% to 20%+ on cold leads.

nodes.label: Quality + Quantity Offer Bifurcation
nodes.description: **Framework: Quality + Quantity Offer Bifurcation** — Split a project-based service into two distinct offer tracks: a high-ticket upfront quality package capturing representative ICPs, and a lower-cost recurring quantity package providing fresh, ongoing UGC-style assets — enabling continuity revenue that project-only pricing cannot sustain.

nodes.label: Software Valuation Components
nodes.description: **Framework: Software Valuation Components** — Three features that make software economically valuable at exit: near-zero marginal cost for additional customers (high gross margin), viral growth, and revenue retention (ideally net negative churn via account expansion).

nodes.label: Persuasion vs. Legislation vs. Economics Hierarchy
nodes.description: **Framework: Persuasion vs. Legislation vs. Economics Hierarchy** — A three-tier policy toolkit (legislation, economic incentives, voluntary persuasion) where persuasion uniquely preserves individual optionality and enables distributed adaptation that centralized tools cannot achieve.

nodes.label: Placebo Libertarianism
nodes.description: **Framework: Placebo Libertarianism** — Offering a structured menu of behaviorally equivalent options (e.g., choose any 3 of 5 actions) so individuals feel autonomous choice, increasing adoption and evangelism relative to mandated single behaviors.

nodes.label: Model Distortion Cycle
nodes.description: **Framework: Model Distortion Cycle** — When a model or metric becomes widely used, behavior optimizes toward the metric rather than the underlying reality the metric was designed to measure, progressively distorting the domain it was meant to describe.

nodes.label: Four-Component Mental Toughness Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Four-Component Mental Toughness Model** — Mental toughness decomposed into four measurable behavioral dimensions: tolerance (how much hardship before behavior changes), fortitude (how severe the behavior change is), resilience (how quickly one returns to baseline), and adaptability (whether the new baseline is higher or lower than the old one).

nodes.label: Trauma as Permanent Behavior Change
nodes.description: **Framework: Trauma as Permanent Behavior Change** — Trauma defined operationally as a permanent change of behavior resulting from an aversive stimulus, removing the valence assumption; trauma can be positive (new baseline higher) or negative (new baseline lower).

nodes.label: Demand Unlock Decision Tree
nodes.description: **Framework: Demand Unlock Decision Tree** — A three-branch diagnostic for demand-constrained businesses: (1) open a new channel, (2) lower CAC via CRO or better creative/offer, or (3) simply spend more on existing channel.

nodes.label: UGC Content Loop
nodes.description: **Framework: UGC Content Loop** — A decentralized content engine in which customers are incentivized to post trip montages in exchange for gated content, generating 20-30 videos per week that are tested organically and the winners are scaled as paid ads.

nodes.label: Kaleidoscope Creative Variation
nodes.description: **Framework: Kaleidoscope Creative Variation** — Take one winning creative and generate 20-30 visual variations via AI filters, color treatments, cartoonization, and motion conversion, then blast all variants to find new winners without changing the underlying offer or copy.

nodes.label: Lead Scoring by Dual Qualifier
nodes.description: **Framework: Lead Scoring by Dual Qualifier** — Score and prioritize inbound leads by two qualifying variables (e.g., credit card spend and vacation spend), calling two-for-two matches first, one-for-one matches second, and zero-for-two last.

nodes.label: Damaging Admissions Front-Load
nodes.description: **Framework: Damaging Admissions Front-Load** — Open a sales call by proactively listing every limitation and reason the product will not work for the prospect, before stating benefits, so the prospect self-qualifies and believes the benefits when stated.

nodes.label: Custom-Order Sales Flow
nodes.description: **Framework: Custom-Order Sales Flow** — A four-stage sequential funnel for converting DIY railing browsers into custom-order buyers: (1) form opt-in, (2) pre-call VSL with price anchoring and BANT qualification via SMS, (3) consultative phone close with on-call discount incentive, (4) card capture on the call.

nodes.label: Long-Term Email Nurture Structure
nodes.plugin: 2x Weekly Email Cadence with Rotating Themes
nodes.description: **Framework: Long-Term Email Nurture Structure** — A recurring two-to-three-times-per-week email cadence rotating three content themes: (1) before/after transformation photos, (2) cool project showcases, (3) FAQ objection-breakers — each email structured as subject line, immediate visual reward, CTA link, and PS.
nodes.parent_id: concept:2x Weekly Email Cadence with Rotating Themes
nodes.topic: 2x Weekly Email Cadence with Rotating Themes

nodes.label: Virtuous Cycle of Pricing
nodes.description: **Framework: Virtuous Cycle of Pricing** — Raising price increases emotional investment, which increases perceived value, which improves results, which decreases customer demandingness and generates more revenue to fund delivery — a self-reinforcing loop.

nodes.label: Demand-Constrained vs Supply-Constrained Diagnosis
nodes.description: **Framework: Demand-Constrained vs Supply-Constrained Diagnosis** — Before investing in lead generation, determine whether doubling lead flow would be absorbed (demand-constrained) or collapse fulfillment (supply-constrained); only demand-constrained businesses should invest in more leads.

nodes.label: Affiliate Offer Architecture (Lead-Magnet Upsell)
nodes.description: **Framework: Affiliate Offer Architecture (Lead-Magnet Upsell)** — Structure affiliate deals so the partner sells or gives away the lower-ticket service, keeps all that revenue, and the affiliate business upsells into its core higher-ticket offer on the back end — converting the partner's cost of acquisition into the affiliate's effective CAC.

nodes.label: Warm Process on Cold Leads Inversion
nodes.description: **Framework: Warm Process on Cold Leads Inversion** — Cold acquisition processes work on both cold and warm leads; warm-only processes fail on cold leads. The safe default is always the cold process because running warm leads through a cold process does not hurt conversion, but the reverse leaves cold leads unsold.

nodes.label: Soft Handoff Transition Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Soft Handoff Transition Model** — Instead of a 100% immediate transfer of clients to a new practitioner, the founder remains nominally in the loop (via shared notes, occasional messages, no live calls) while the new hire handles day-to-day delivery, reducing churn risk and theft risk during the transition.

nodes.label: Three Cash-Flow Pull-Forward Levers
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Cash-Flow Pull-Forward Levers** — A three-part sequence for a capital-constrained product business to accelerate cash collection before acquiring a major asset: (1) renegotiate supplier payment terms to net 30/60/90, (2) use pre-orders to collect revenue before production, (3) maximize existing volume capacity to generate operating cash flow.

nodes.label: Attention-to-Perception Bridge
nodes.description: **Framework: Attention-to-Perception Bridge** — Changing what you focus attention on (the frame or narrative) restructures how you perceive a situation, which restructures your emotional and behavioral response.

nodes.label: Mental Accounting and Prepaid Cost Absorption
nodes.description: **Framework: Mental Accounting and Prepaid Cost Absorption** — Costs that are paid upfront and mentally committed (stored value cards, advance hotel/airline payments) feel like sunk costs, making subsequent expenditures feel smaller than their absolute price.

nodes.label: Abductive Inference Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Abductive Inference Framework** — A problem-solving method (named by Charles Sanders Peirce) that begins from a strange observed fact and asks: what would have to be true for this to occur? Requires imagination and hypothesis, unlike induction (data to rule) or deduction (rule to conclusion). Used in detective work, Darwin's theory of evolution, and Fleming's discovery of penicillin.

nodes.label: Post-Rationalization Asymmetry
nodes.description: **Framework: Post-Rationalization Asymmetry** — The observation that the set of ideas that can be validated after discovery (post-rationalized) is substantially larger than the set that can be generated through logical pre-reasoning alone; creativity expands the viable solution space beyond what deduction can reach.

nodes.label: Bee Waggle Dance Exploration Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Bee Waggle Dance Exploration Model** — Bees use a waggle dance to communicate known food sources, but a significant fraction (~20%) of bees ignore the dance and explore independently. Evolutionary modeling showed this inefficiency is adaptive: exploratory bees prevent the colony from becoming trapped in a local maximum and enable adaptation to changing environments.

nodes.label: Two Ways to Sell a Product
nodes.description: **Framework: Two Ways to Sell a Product** — All product selling reduces to two poles: mass social normalisation (everybody buys this, so it must be good — the Coca-Cola model) or exclusivity signalling (very few people buy this, so it must be good — the French luxury goods model). Television excels at the former; precision direct marketing excels at the latter.

nodes.label: Targeting-Communication Cancellation Trap
nodes.description: **Framework: Targeting-Communication Cancellation Trap** — Combining high precision targeting with low-impact communication format cancels the benefit of each: precision targeting creates value by enabling expensive, high-impact outreach to a small qualified audience; cheap digital delivery destroys that value by making the outreach feel mass-market and easy-to-ignore.

nodes.label: Industry Belief Inertia
nodes.description: **Framework: Industry Belief Inertia** — Systems of false or questionable beliefs persist in industries when consensus makes dissent socially/professionally costly, not because evidence supports them.

nodes.label: Direct Response Doom Loop
nodes.description: **Framework: Direct Response Doom Loop** — A named cycle in paid-media e-commerce where revenue scales until CAC rises and gross margins compress until the business is a high-liability, low-margin operation that requires perpetual revenue just to sustain the team.

nodes.label: Brand Loop
nodes.description: **Framework: Brand Loop** — The virtuous cycle in which a strong brand promise attracts true believers (influencers, affiliates), the product reinforces that promise on delivery, and each satisfied customer deepens the brand rather than diluting it — enabling exits at premium multiples rather than product-arbitrage multiples.

nodes.label: Design for Extremes, Not Average
nodes.description: **Framework: Design for Extremes, Not Average** — Products and solutions designed for extreme or unusual consumer segments often achieve mainstream adoption; designing for a single representative average person creates dead ends.

nodes.label: Lateral Category Analysis
nodes.description: **Framework: Lateral Category Analysis** — A problem-solving approach that recognizes most complex problems have already been solved in different domains, requiring transfer of solutions across category boundaries.

nodes.label: TRIZ Problem Definition Linkage
nodes.description: **Framework: TRIZ Problem Definition Linkage** — A framework for identifying how poor problem definitions create false constraints that prevent recognition of solutions already existing in other domains.

nodes.label: Obedient Bee vs. Rogue Bee Allocation
nodes.description: **Framework: Obedient Bee vs. Rogue Bee Allocation** — Organizations should split employee effort between exploitation (obedient bees following known directions) and exploration (rogue bees taking random journeys), with separate ROI thresholds for each, because over-compliance traps the system in a local maximum and starves it of new discoveries.

nodes.label: Time-Average vs. Ensemble-Average Growth
nodes.description: **Framework: Time-Average vs. Ensemble-Average Growth** — In multiplicative systems (finance, life, business), consistent low-variance growth compounds to a higher terminal value than high-variance growth with the same arithmetic mean, because a single catastrophic loss in a multiplicative chain destroys all prior gains. Formalized by Ole Peters and Murray Gell-Mann.

nodes.label: Lateral Category Transfer (TRIZ)
nodes.description: **Framework: Lateral Category Transfer (TRIZ)** — Most complex problems have already been solved in a different domain; the innovation move is to identify the solved version in the adjacent domain and transfer it, rather than reinvent within the current domain. Named practice from Soviet TRIZ methodology.

nodes.label: Blue Mountain Paths Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Blue Mountain Paths Framework** — A decision model in which multiple distinct routes all reach the same destination (the prize); the mistake is spending time at the base choosing rather than climbing any of them.

nodes.label: Placebo-Plus-Drug Optimization Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Placebo-Plus-Drug Optimization Framework** — Rather than subtracting the placebo effect from drug efficacy in trials, medical and commercial value creation should maximize both the intrinsic effect and the perceptual/contextual effect simultaneously, as they may multiply rather than merely add.

nodes.label: Austrian School Value Definition
nodes.description: **Framework: Austrian School Value Definition** — Value is whatever someone is prepared to pay for, regardless of whether it originates in intrinsic product properties or psychological/contextual framing; the distinction between manufacturing value and marketing value is meaningless from the standpoint of economic outcomes.

nodes.label: McNamara Fallacy (Quantitative Bias)
nodes.description: **Framework: McNamara Fallacy (Quantitative Bias)** — Measuring only what is objectively quantifiable (SI units: weight, time, speed) while discounting subjective improvements systematically distorts strategy; named for Robert McNamara's use of kill counts in the Vietnam War.

nodes.label: Meaning-Emotion-Behavior Chain
nodes.description: **Framework: Meaning-Emotion-Behavior Chain** — Human decision-making follows a fixed sequence: context changes meaning, meaning triggers emotion, emotion drives behavior, behavior is followed by post-hoc rationalization. People do not respond to things; they respond to things-in-context.

nodes.label: Costly Signaling Theory
nodes.description: **Framework: Costly Signaling Theory** — A signal is only reliable — and therefore persuasive — when it consumes a resource that is in short supply (money, creativity, effort, skill), making it too costly to fake. The framework, derived from Amotz Zahavi's handicap principle in evolutionary biology, explains why expensive or difficult communication is trusted and cheap communication is discounted.

nodes.label: Rider-and-Elephant Dual-Process Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Rider-and-Elephant Dual-Process Model** — Jonathan Haidt's model in which conscious reasoning (the rider) sits atop unconscious instinct (the elephant). The rider generates post-hoc rationalizations; the elephant actually drives behavior. Effective communication must be written for the elephant, not just the rider.

nodes.label: Faith-in-Futurity Signaling
nodes.description: **Framework: Faith-in-Futurity Signaling** — Upfront expenditure on communication or physical commitment (advertising spend, premium print, engagement rings, bank architecture) functions as a credible proof of long-term intent because a short-term actor would never pay such costs voluntarily.

nodes.label: Tamagotchi Microbiome Frame
nodes.description: **Framework: Tamagotchi Microbiome Frame** — A mental model for understanding diet: the gut microbiome is treated as a living creature (like a Tamagotchi) that must be actively fed the right inputs; this reframes eating from deprivation-avoidance to additive caretaking.

nodes.label: Good Bugs / Bad Bugs Spectrum
nodes.plugin: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking
nodes.description: **Framework: Good Bugs / Bad Bugs Spectrum** — ZOE's working taxonomy that classifies gut bacteria into approximately 50 beneficial and 50 harmful species, providing a simplified vocabulary for communicating the microbiome's role in health outcomes.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking
nodes.topic: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking

nodes.label: Parallel Funnel Structure
nodes.description: **Framework: Parallel Funnel Structure** — A mirror of the demand-generation funnel built for talent: app-gen, app-nurture, interviewing, onboarding, and retention/ascension for salespeople, running concurrently with the lead-gen funnel.

nodes.label: Uninformed Optimism to Breakthrough Arc
nodes.description: **Framework: Uninformed Optimism to Breakthrough Arc** — A four-stage emotional arc in any hard endeavor: (1) uninformed optimism, (2) informed pessimism, (3) valley of despair (where most quit), (4) upside and goal achievement. Most people exit at stage 3 by starting a new cycle at stage 1.

nodes.label: Declarative vs Procedural Knowledge
nodes.description: **Framework: Declarative vs Procedural Knowledge** — Two distinct knowledge types: declarative (knowing about — facts, concepts, how something works) versus procedural (knowing how — the embodied ability to execute). Declarative knowledge is commonly mistaken for procedural, causing false confidence.

nodes.label: Three Outcomes of Difficulty
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Outcomes of Difficulty** — Every hard endeavor resolves in exactly one of three ways: (1) you quit, (2) external circumstances improve (it gets easier), or (3) you develop internally (you get harder). No fourth outcome exists; difficulty always ends.

nodes.label: Brand Bounce vs Brand Extension
nodes.description: **Framework: Brand Bounce vs Brand Extension** — A brand extension stays within the same category (e.g., a light variant); a brand bounce moves into a completely different category and uses the brand as instant credentials in that new space.

nodes.label: Peak-End Rule Applied to Customer Experience
nodes.plugin: Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP
nodes.description: **Framework: Peak-End Rule Applied to Customer Experience** — How an experience ends has a disproportionate effect on the memory of the entire experience; excellence at the close point (e.g., coffee at meal end) carries outsized weight relative to the preceding sequence.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP
nodes.topic: Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP

nodes.label: Minority Rule in Product and Menu Design
nodes.description: **Framework: Minority Rule in Product and Menu Design** — When one group will only accept option A and another group accepts either A or B, the entire system defaults to A regardless of majority preference — meaning intransigent minorities set the standard for the whole.

nodes.label: Commercial Innovation Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Commercial Innovation Framework** — A class of innovation distinct from product innovation: changing how something is sold, priced, packaged, or bundled (e.g., Amazon Prime, Persil rail tickets) to unlock value without altering the product itself.

nodes.label: Pick Your Price
nodes.description: **Framework: Pick Your Price** — A three-stage offer structure: (1) market the offer as free, (2) at checkout present three donation/payment tiers (small/medium/large) with escalating bonuses, (3) end with a payment method question and silence. The framing attributes bonuses to staff, not the business, to exploit the consumer preference for paying employees over businesses.

nodes.label: Scenting the Soap
nodes.description: **Framework: Scenting the Soap** — Attach a selfish individual benefit (vanity, social fear) to a prosocial behavior so people adopt the behavior for private reasons and the social benefit emerges as a byproduct.

nodes.label: Kano Excitement Attribute
nodes.description: **Framework: Kano Excitement Attribute** — Norio Kano's model distinguishing threshold functional attributes (must-haves) from excitement attributes (delighters) that disproportionately determine purchase choice even when functionally trivial.

nodes.label: Benign Bullshit
nodes.description: **Framework: Benign Bullshit** — A reframing device that attaches an emotionally resonant but functionally irrelevant superlative or story to a product or place, converting it from a utilitarian object into a destination or desirable identity.

nodes.label: Expectation-Experience Alignment
nodes.description: **Framework: Expectation-Experience Alignment** — The quality of an experience is determined not by objective properties but by the congruence between advance expectations and actual delivery.

nodes.label: C-L-O-S-E-R Formula
nodes.description: **Framework: C-L-O-S-E-R Formula** — A six-step in-person sales framework: Clarify why they are there, Label them with the problem, Overview their past pains, Sell the vacation (outcome), Explain away concerns, and Reinforce their decision.

nodes.label: Wedding Cake Gym Profit Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Wedding Cake Gym Profit Model** — A three-tier revenue architecture (large-group training, semi-privates, supplements) where each tier carries both icing (front-end cash) and cake (recurring EFT), designed to accommodate the full customer buying curve and capture multiple spending wallets.

nodes.label: Gym Profit Levers
nodes.description: **Framework: Gym Profit Levers** — Three macro levers that together transform gym profitability: Price Levers (membership price, billing cycle, membership levels), Capacity Levers (session duration, membership limits, attendance spread, physical space, exercise selection), and Overhead Levers (number of sessions, trainer hours, trainer pay).

nodes.label: Five Horsemen of Retention
nodes.description: **Framework: Five Horsemen of Retention** — Five evidence-based retention tactics for membership businesses: Reach-Outs (personal touch every 14 days), Attendance Tracking (weekly red-flag identification), Handwritten Cards (at sign-up, referral requests, milestones), Member Events (every 21 days), and Exit Interviews (re-sell using C-L-O-S-E-R).

nodes.label: Client-Financed Acquisition
nodes.description: **Framework: Client-Financed Acquisition** — A growth model in which a high-ticket front-end offer generates more cash on Day 1 than the cost of the leads that produced it, creating a negative acquisition cost and eliminating the need for a marketing budget.

nodes.label: Ideal Customer Life Cycle
nodes.description: **Framework: Ideal Customer Life Cycle** — Four sequential customer milestones gym owners should deliberately engineer: Connect (form a relationship quickly), Refer/Testify (earn social proof and referrals), Testify/Refer (order may flip), and Ascend (upsell to higher-tier service or adjacent product).

nodes.label: Content Graph vs. Social Graph
nodes.plugin: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience
nodes.description: **Framework: Content Graph vs. Social Graph** — A two-axis model distinguishing platforms that serve content based on your social network (social graph) from platforms that serve content based on interest signals regardless of social connections (content graph); TikTok operates on the content graph, which enables discovery of content the user did not know they would want.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience
nodes.topic: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience

nodes.label: Single-Highest-Leverage Activity Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Single-Highest-Leverage Activity Framework** — Identify the one activity that, if done alone, accomplishes all other objectives; hire people for everything else and concentrate founder time entirely on that activity.

nodes.label: Four Acquisition Channels
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Acquisition Channels** — Four non-referral channels for getting clients: paid ads, organic content, cold outreach, and affiliate/partner networks.

nodes.label: Sales God to Sales Training God Identity Shift
nodes.description: **Framework: Sales God to Sales Training God Identity Shift** — A two-phase identity reframe for founder-dependent sales businesses: Phase 1 (sales god) — founder closes deals personally and maximizes individual output; Phase 2 (sales training god) — founder codifies their winning behaviors into teachable scripts and systems, and judges themselves by how well they can replicate their performance in others rather than by their own closing numbers.

nodes.label: Guaranteed Path + Fast Path Market Entry
nodes.description: **Framework: Guaranteed Path + Fast Path Market Entry** — A two-track strategy for entering a new local market: one track is the reliable organic/outreach playbook (guaranteed path); the other is paid ads at low daily budget ($100-200/day) to accelerate learning (fast path). Both run concurrently.

nodes.label: CPA Channel Expansion Model
nodes.description: **Framework: CPA Channel Expansion Model** — Replace dependence on 3-4 high-value referral partners by expanding to 30-40 CPAs, converting each into an independent pipeline that collectively 10x lead flow without changing the core offer.

nodes.label: Sales Director Role Definition
nodes.description: **Framework: Sales Director Role Definition** — A sales director's primary function is culture maintenance and daily sales training — not closing deals or carrying specialized domain knowledge about the product being sold.

nodes.label: Scientific Attribution Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Scientific Attribution Model** — A hybrid attribution rule: if conversion happens within 30 days of a touchpoint, credit goes to last touch; if more than 30 days, credit goes to first touch. Designed to avoid over-indexing on direct response (last-touch only) or brand (first-touch only).

nodes.label: Delivery-Change Moral High Ground Pitch
nodes.description: **Framework: Delivery-Change Moral High Ground Pitch** — A three-part reframe for announcing a delivery reduction: (1) acknowledge you have been falling short of a stated promise, (2) position the change as restoring integrity rather than cutting service, (3) list reasons the new format benefits clients, making it socially costly for any client to object.

nodes.label: Big Head Long Tail Pricing
nodes.description: **Framework: Big Head Long Tail Pricing** — Charge a large upfront fee for the primary value (skill or transformation), then price the continuity component much lower as a near-free network access fee, separating one-time value from consumable recurring value.

nodes.label: Five-Part Sales Training Rotation
nodes.plugin: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence
nodes.description: **Framework: Five-Part Sales Training Rotation** — Break sales team training into five rotating daily segments: intro, discovery, offer, objections, looping, and a fifth wild-card slot for the current high-priority skill gap; rotate through all segments to keep every part of the script sharp.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence
nodes.topic: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

nodes.label: Three-Bucket Avatar Segmentation
nodes.description: **Framework: Three-Bucket Avatar Segmentation** — Segment prospects by three independent axes: demographics (who they look like), quantifiables (business size and financials), and behaviors (actions correlated with activation and retention); only sell to avatars that score well on all three.

nodes.label: Management Diamond
nodes.description: **Framework: Management Diamond** — A diagnostic model for identifying why a person is not executing: they don't know they need to do it, don't know how, don't know when, have something blocking them, or lack motivation.

nodes.label: Inbound/Outbound Separation
nodes.description: **Framework: Inbound/Outbound Separation** — Inbound and outbound sales must be structurally separate teams; inbound is a reward earned by top closers, not a starting point for new salespeople.

nodes.label: Recruiting as Volume Game
nodes.description: **Framework: Recruiting as Volume Game** — When talent is the binding constraint, the primary lever is 3-10x outreach volume and recruiter headcount, not recruiter quality alone — treated identically to a sales volume problem.

nodes.label: Talent Investment ROI Math
nodes.description: **Framework: Talent Investment ROI Math** — A three-variable calculation (cost of hire, gross profit per hire, number of hires needed) that frames a recruiting budget as a capital-allocation decision with a stated payback multiple.

nodes.label: 20% Guaranteed Cost of Change
nodes.description: **Framework: 20% Guaranteed Cost of Change** — Every change to a running business incurs a guaranteed ~20% performance decrement before any gains accrue; this floor means a change requires 50%+ upside to justify the certain downside.

nodes.label: Defend-the-Perimeter Scaling Metaphor
nodes.description: **Framework: Defend-the-Perimeter Scaling Metaphor** — A spatial analogy mapping business scope to physical defense area: the larger the territory a single person tries to defend, the less effective their defense becomes; a founder spreading across multiple business layers is analogous to guarding an entire city block solo.

nodes.label: Creative Agency Pivot: Volume Over Premium
nodes.description: **Framework: Creative Agency Pivot: Volume Over Premium** — A two-pole strategic choice for AI ad production businesses: pursue true enterprise at $500K with the AI kept hidden, OR pursue mid-market clients spending $100K+/month in ads by replacing their entire creative team with high-volume AI-generated ads at a monthly retainer.

nodes.label: Four-Problem Upstream Diagnosis
nodes.description: **Framework: Four-Problem Upstream Diagnosis** — A four-part diagnostic for revenue-plateau businesses: avatar clarity, offer structure, positioning, and messaging — in that order of fix priority.

nodes.label: Map Clients to Product Suite (Not Product to Clients)
nodes.description: **Framework: Map Clients to Product Suite (Not Product to Clients)** — Rather than customizing every offer to each client's venue, templatize a product suite (e.g., three core configurations) and map inbound clients to the nearest template.

nodes.label: Global vs. Local Positioning Frame
nodes.description: **Framework: Global vs. Local Positioning Frame** — For corporate or B2B buyers who will try to commoditize the offer, reframe the value conversation from line-item cost to total business cost (time, switching costs, headcount waste), so that price comparison becomes impossible.

nodes.label: Two-Path Exit Decision
nodes.description: **Framework: Two-Path Exit Decision** — When a service business has both an operator-facing education or coaching arm and a corporate/studio arm, the founder must choose between path A (information/coaching = higher annual income, very hard to sell) and path B (corporate brand = lower annual income, easier to sell at exit); there is no viable third path.

nodes.label: Equity Decomposition Framework (Cash Flow, Sale, Risk, Control)
nodes.description: **Framework: Equity Decomposition Framework (Cash Flow, Sale, Risk, Control)** — A four-part breakdown of what equity actually consists of (cash flow, sale upside, risk, and control) used to identify which components an employee actually wants so non-dilutive alternatives can be offered in their place.

nodes.label: OTE Reverse-Engineering for Profit Share
nodes.description: **Framework: OTE Reverse-Engineering for Profit Share** — A compensation design process that starts from desired on-target earnings for a role, then back-calculates the profit-share percentage required to hit that OTE at expected profit levels, rather than picking an arbitrary percentage.

nodes.label: The Swamp
nodes.description: **Framework: The Swamp** — A 1-3M revenue band where thin margins (10-20%) make hiring an operator impossible without absorbing the majority of available profit, trapping founders in a double-bind of either working two full-time roles or taking a large bet that destroys profitability.

nodes.label: Sales Motion Fix Before Pricing Fix
nodes.description: **Framework: Sales Motion Fix Before Pricing Fix** — A two-step repair sequence: fix the in-person close process first (order 1), then raise prices (order 2); reversing the sequence is ineffective because a broken sales motion causes the founder to attribute low conversion to price, when the real driver is process.

nodes.label: Direct Response Doom Loop
nodes.description: **Framework: Direct Response Doom Loop** — A compressing cycle in which e-commerce revenue scales via paid media while margins simultaneously shrink until the business becomes a high-liability, low-margin operation that must keep selling just to sustain its cost base.

nodes.label: Eugene Schwartz Awareness Pyramid
nodes.description: **Framework: Eugene Schwartz Awareness Pyramid** — A five-level customer awareness hierarchy (Unaware, Problem Aware, Solution Aware, Product Aware, Most Aware) that determines what hook and click journey a prospect requires; bridge pages convert colder audiences by stepping them up through levels before reaching a sales page.

nodes.label: Brand Completion Loop
nodes.description: **Framework: Brand Completion Loop** — A virtuous cycle in which a strong brand promise attracts customers, the product experience either reinforces or destroys that promise, and reinforcement deepens brand equity, enabling premium pricing and affiliate recruitment.

nodes.label: Marketing as Filtration System
nodes.description: **Framework: Marketing as Filtration System** — Marketing finds ideal buyers who already exist rather than educating or converting beginners into ideal buyers; the message and medium select for the avatar, not transform them.

nodes.label: Nail It Then Scale It
nodes.description: **Framework: Nail It Then Scale It** — A sequencing rule for brick-and-mortar expansion: prove that a single unit operates at sustained performance without the founder before committing capital to a second location.

nodes.label: Founder-Absence Test (Three-to-Six Month)
nodes.description: **Framework: Founder-Absence Test (Three-to-Six Month)** — A three-to-six month period in which the founder fully withdraws from day-to-day operations to confirm the GM can sustain or grow the business independently; failure during this window blocks expansion.

nodes.label: ACQ Universe Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: ACQ Universe Framework** — A layered monetization architecture: free media generates attention, low-ticket conversions (books, email list, School) capture contact info, a tiered advisory practice converts business owners to high-ticket, and excess capital redeploys into real estate, ventures, and private equity — all anchored by one brand credibility promise.

nodes.label: Disney Analogy for B2B Media Company
nodes.description: **Framework: Disney Analogy for B2B Media Company** — Maps Acquisition.com revenue streams to Disney properties: brand = Disney Studios, ACQ Network = Disney+, Advisory Practice = theme parks, School = Star Wars/Marvel franchise investments, insurance/sales AI/lending = future spokes — illustrating how a single brand supports multiple distinct monetization arms.

nodes.label: One-Level-Up Channel Strategy
nodes.description: **Framework: One-Level-Up Channel Strategy** — Instead of acquiring end customers directly, acquire the intermediary (agency, guru, mentor) who already has those customers, capturing higher LTV via onboarding fees, per-customer fees, and recurring top-line percentage.

nodes.label: Logic-First vs. Empirical Testing Tradeoff
nodes.description: **Framework: Logic-First vs. Empirical Testing Tradeoff** — When decisions are constrained to only those that make sense in advance, high-value solutions are systematically missed because their value proposition is counterintuitive.

nodes.label: Choose Your Regrets Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Choose Your Regrets Framework** — Christopher Hitchens' principle that because opportunity cost is structurally unavoidable in all human choices, regrets are inevitable rather than the result of bad decisions; the only agency available is choosing which regrets to accept.

nodes.label: Close-Rate Pricing Gap Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Close-Rate Pricing Gap Framework** — A five-tier scale mapping close-rate ranges to the implied pricing multiple still available; 80%+ close rate = 3-4x multiple remaining; 30-40% = appropriately priced; below 30% = execution problem.

nodes.label: Service Pricing Virtuous Cycle
nodes.description: **Framework: Service Pricing Virtuous Cycle** — A closed loop in which higher price enables higher gross margins, which fund better talent, which deliver better service, which improve reputation, which drive demand, which justify higher price.

nodes.label: Learning to Try Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Learning to Try Framework** — A meta-skill built by committing all discretionary effort, money, and time to one domain for an extended daily period; once internalized, the skill of sustained commitment transfers across domains (saxophone, tennis, content creation) because skill acquisition follows the same pattern everywhere.

nodes.label: Tolerance as First Component of Mental Toughness
nodes.description: **Framework: Tolerance as First Component of Mental Toughness** — A model of mental toughness whose first component, tolerance, measures how long a person maintains their intended behavior before hardship causes a behavioral change (the fuse length), distinct from pain tolerance or pain ignorance.

nodes.label: Felix Dennis Eleven Levels of Wealth
nodes.plugin: Wealth Tiers and Diminishing Marginal Returns
nodes.description: **Framework: Felix Dennis Eleven Levels of Wealth** — Felix Dennis's framework from his book on wealth breaks affluence into 11 tiers, asserting that only at $400M+ liquid does a person achieve true financial freedom where they can do whatever they want without constraint.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Wealth Tiers and Diminishing Marginal Returns
nodes.topic: Wealth Tiers and Diminishing Marginal Returns

nodes.label: Inspired Internet Pledge (Three-Principle Framework)
nodes.description: **Framework: Inspired Internet Pledge (Three-Principle Framework)** — A three-part industry commitment: (1) Create for Well-Being — understand what content attributes correlate with well-being; (2) Listen and Act — gather experiential data from users who have experienced online harm; (3) Commit to Openness — share safety learnings across the industry rather than treating user well-being as a competitive differentiator.

nodes.label: Inspiration-to-Realization Funnel
nodes.description: **Framework: Inspiration-to-Realization Funnel** — Pinterest's platform design moves users from open-ended inspiration (unbranded search, mood boards) through narrowing intent to final purchase action — a full-funnel trajectory unique among digital platforms because it begins before the user has formed a specific product intent.

nodes.label: Four-Strategy Compounding Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Four-Strategy Compounding Framework** — Alex Hormozi's four-part personal finance strategy: (1) increase income, (2) reduce spending, (3) invest faster/earlier, (4) invest in income-earning skills as the highest-ROI lever.

nodes.label: Skill Bridge Metaphor
nodes.description: **Framework: Skill Bridge Metaphor** — Skills are individual bridge segments; missing links prevent income from crossing to the other side. Each purchase adds a segment, and no single skill alone spans the gap — the full chain compounds.

nodes.label: Learning Budget Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Learning Budget Model** — Allocate a fixed monthly percentage of income (1–10%) as a mandatory spending budget for skill experiments and education; the mechanism is forced experimentation, not optional learning.

nodes.label: Do Epic Then Talk Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Do Epic Then Talk Framework** — Two-step sequence for building credibility and providing value: (1) achieve something notable or accumulate effort-proof, then (2) talk about what you learned from it.

nodes.label: V-Shape Rebound Toolkit
nodes.description: **Framework: V-Shape Rebound Toolkit** — A named collection of cognitive tools (cosmic relevance, veteran frame) whose shared purpose is to compress the time from an aversive event back to baseline behavior, making recovery as rapid and V-shaped as possible.

nodes.label: Veteran Frame
nodes.description: **Framework: Veteran Frame** — A perspective tool: imagine the same inconvenience occurring one thousand times in a row; identify how you would feel on the thousandth occurrence; then recognize that feeling is available on the first occurrence because the circumstance itself has not changed.

nodes.label: Cosmic Relevance Frame
nodes.description: **Framework: Cosmic Relevance Frame** — A perspective tool that situates a personal setback within its astronomical context (planet orbiting a sun inside a galaxy inside an ever-expanding universe) to instantly reduce the perceived magnitude of the setback to near zero.

nodes.label: Behavioral Change Intensity Scale
nodes.description: **Framework: Behavioral Change Intensity Scale** — A two-pole axis measuring how much behavior changes after a person's tolerance threshold is exceeded: high fortitude = minimal behavior change; low fortitude = severe, life-disrupting behavior change.

nodes.label: Six Principles for Building Capacity Before Knowing What to Do
nodes.description: **Framework: Six Principles for Building Capacity Before Knowing What to Do** — A six-part framework for ambitious people who lack direction: (1) build physical and financial capacity, (2) save money to buy optionality, (3) add and practice skills, (4) build an audience without a product, (5) build a waitlist before building the thing, (6) expand luck surface area via networking and geographic proximity.

nodes.label: Skill Stacking Multiplier
nodes.description: **Framework: Skill Stacking Multiplier** — Each new skill acquired multiplies the value of all previously held skills; the portfolio grows super-linearly because each layer has the prior layers as prerequisites.

nodes.label: Conscious Trade Accounting Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Conscious Trade Accounting Framework** — Every life outcome requires a conscious trade of something valued (time, safety, experience); the framework asks two questions: what am I trading, and what am I trading it for.

nodes.label: Upside-Downside Asymmetry Frame
nodes.description: **Framework: Upside-Downside Asymmetry Frame** — Downside is bounded (survivable worst-case) while upside is unbounded; therefore rational action tilts toward taking bets rather than avoiding them.

nodes.label: RFP Frame + Value Frame Stack
nodes.description: **Framework: RFP Frame + Value Frame Stack** — Every B2B sales conversation operates on two simultaneous layers: the RFP frame (commodity, price-comparison, minimum viable compliance) and the value frame (holistic business impact, ROI, total cost of risk). Winning requires satisfying the RFP floor while differentiating on the value ceiling.

nodes.label: Case Study Close
nodes.description: **Framework: Case Study Close** — In procurement-driven (RFP) sales contexts, attach a peer-company case study to every bid that demonstrates the most analogous client's outcome on the exact value drivers (speed, risk reduction, total cost) the buyer cares about; the prior client's voice displaces price-only comparison.

nodes.label: Flip to Motivated Buyer Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Flip to Motivated Buyer Framework** — When sellers are structurally reluctant (frozen market), redirect sourcing effort toward buyers with forced timelines (e.g., 1031 exchange deadlines) who must transact regardless of market conditions, and use their urgency to extract seller-side deals.

nodes.label: Community-as-CRM Asset Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Community-as-CRM Asset Framework** — Build a gated community of your exact target avatar (e.g., multifamily owners in one metro), position yourself as the gating function, and over time create a proprietary CRM that is both an ongoing deal-flow engine and a sellable business asset.

nodes.label: Commission-to-Consulting Revenue Conversion
nodes.description: **Framework: Commission-to-Consulting Revenue Conversion** — Replace variable transaction-based commission income with a fixed annual consulting retainer; subsidize the retainer with a deeply discounted commission rate so the recurring income is pulled forward while clients perceive total cost as lower.

nodes.label: Conviction-Trust Sales Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Conviction-Trust Sales Framework** — Two necessary conditions for any sale: (1) the seller must have near-total conviction in their product, and (2) the prospect must develop enough trust in the seller that the seller's conviction transfers to the prospect.

nodes.label: Consultative Sales Sequence
nodes.description: **Framework: Consultative Sales Sequence** — A structured conversation sequence: (1) why are they there / what is the problem, (2) what have they tried and failed, (3) why your product is different from what failed, (4) ask permission to explain the product, (5) explain through experiences (not features), using analogies, (6) close.

nodes.label: No-Based Close
nodes.description: **Framework: No-Based Close** — Framing the close as a soft opt-out question (e.g., 'Would you mind?') rather than a hard yes-demand, exploiting natural communication dynamics where 'I don't mind' is easier to say than 'yes'.

nodes.label: Content-First to Paid Ads Sequencing
nodes.description: **Framework: Content-First to Paid Ads Sequencing** — A three-step acquisition sequence: (1) post organic before/after content, (2) identify the best-performing piece, (3) attach a CTA and run it as a paid ad.

nodes.label: Leaky Bucket Retention Diagnosis
nodes.description: **Framework: Leaky Bucket Retention Diagnosis** — Track monthly joins versus cancels to classify a recurring-revenue business as growing, flat, or declining; MRR grows only when new members exceed churned members.

nodes.label: Day-90 / Month-6 Retention Milestones
nodes.description: **Framework: Day-90 / Month-6 Retention Milestones** — Two tactical milestones that predict long-term retention: surviving day 90 cuts monthly churn roughly in half; surviving month 6 cuts it by ~5x again, because churn drops from 20%+ in months 1-3 to ~10% at day 90, then to ~2% by month 6.

nodes.label: Snakes and Ladders Onboarding
nodes.description: **Framework: Snakes and Ladders Onboarding** — Remove snakes (friction, confusion, overwhelm) and front-load ladders (the stickiest value moments) in onboarding; new members should hit a fast win within the first 24 hours.

nodes.label: Lead-with-Free Client Acquisition Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Lead-with-Free Client Acquisition Framework** — A three-stage approach for zero-track-record service founders: (1) offer free engagement (e.g., five calls) to eliminate the proof barrier, (2) win on service quality and aligned incentive signaling, (3) convert to paid or collect testimonial for future paid prospects.

nodes.label: Four Business Shapes
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Business Shapes** — All businesses belong to one of four structural types (e-commerce, service, education/info-media, SaaS) each with a characteristic growth curve, dominant scaling constraint, and competitive moat requirement.

nodes.label: Big Head, Long Tail
nodes.description: **Framework: Big Head, Long Tail** — In education businesses, charge a high one-time price for the core knowledge (big head) and a much lower recurring price for consumable ongoing elements such as community, updated resources, or continued education (long tail); the mismatch in value is what drives churn when the ratio is reversed.

nodes.label: Attraction-Conversion-Delivery
nodes.description: **Framework: Attraction-Conversion-Delivery** — Every business has three structural layers: attraction (getting leads), conversion (closing sales), and delivery (fulfilling the service or product); the layer that requires human labor is the scaling constraint.

nodes.label: Network-vs-Headhunter Role Routing
nodes.description: **Framework: Network-vs-Headhunter Role Routing** — Hire within your own network for roles where you have domain expertise to evaluate candidates; use a paid headhunter for roles where you lack that expertise (e.g., finance, tech, HR at leadership level).

nodes.label: Cringe-as-Status-Play Reframe
nodes.plugin: Shame vs. Guilt: Navigating Social Signals
nodes.description: **Framework: Cringe-as-Status-Play Reframe** — A three-part disambiguation of cringe, shame, and guilt that exposes cringe as a defensive status signal from the observer, not evidence of wrongdoing by the actor.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Shame vs. Guilt: Navigating Social Signals
nodes.topic: Shame vs. Guilt: Navigating Social Signals

nodes.label: Seven-Step Outlearning Process
nodes.description: **Framework: Seven-Step Outlearning Process** — A sequential learning framework: (1) define learning as same-condition behavior change, (2) deconstruct the skill into sub-behaviors, (3) define measurable success criteria, (4) ignore causal explanations and focus on observable inputs/outputs, (5) model top performers by observing what they do, (6) analyze differences between your top 10% attempts and the rest and iterate, (7) repeat with increasing volume.

nodes.label: Skill Deconstruction Hierarchy
nodes.description: **Framework: Skill Deconstruction Hierarchy** — Skills are nested from broad domain labels (business, basketball) down through sub-skills (marketing, dribbling) to atomic observable behaviors that can be tracked and changed; learning requires chunking down to the observable behavioral unit.

nodes.label: Four Investor Acquisition Channels
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Investor Acquisition Channels** — Four discrete paths to reach accredited investors without relying on a personal network: (1) affiliate model (leverage someone else's existing investor audience), (2) paid ads (targeted to accredited investors), (3) content marketing (thought leadership that attracts inbound investor interest), (4) outbound direct contact.

nodes.label: Three Levels of Salesmanship
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Levels of Salesmanship** — A progression from solo selling (Level 1) to recruiting individual salespeople (Level 2) to building and leading a team of salespeople (Level 3); each level requires a distinct identity and skill set.

nodes.label: Downside Tolerance Decision Filter
nodes.description: **Framework: Downside Tolerance Decision Filter** — A four-question sequence for evaluating any new opportunity: (1) What is the upside? (2) What is the downside? (3) Can I live with the downside? (4) How likely is the downside? If the downside is not livable, do not proceed regardless of upside.

nodes.label: Licensing Approval Gate
nodes.description: **Framework: Licensing Approval Gate** — A single prerequisite criterion before permitting expansion into a licensing model: the existing core business must be able to open a new location every quarter using a team that does not include the founder, with zero founder involvement required.

nodes.label: Ham and Garlic Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Ham and Garlic Framework** — Wrap the thing customers need (garlic: continuity) inside the thing they want (ham: a defined short program); the front-end defined offer is a sales vehicle, not the end product.

nodes.label: Two-Pronged Distribution Layer Strategy
nodes.description: **Framework: Two-Pronged Distribution Layer Strategy** — When building a distribution layer, combine (1) a launch campaign for immediate value for affiliates/distributors who have no initial trust, and (2) a long-term retention journey that treats distributors as customers with their own customer journey.

nodes.label: Observable Universe Definitions Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Observable Universe Definitions Framework** — Define every abstract concept in terms of observable, court-admissible behaviors so that all parties share a common referent and communication becomes precise rather than amorphous.

nodes.label: Behavior-Ladder Decomposition
nodes.description: **Framework: Behavior-Ladder Decomposition** — Break abstract trait labels (confident, lazy, patient) into the discrete observable micro-behaviors that cause observers to apply those labels, then address those micro-behaviors directly.

nodes.label: Traffic-Volume Funnel Routing
nodes.description: **Framework: Traffic-Volume Funnel Routing** — Route cold traffic to live call (small volume) or webinar with post-webinar 1-on-1 solicitation (larger volume); funnel structure scales with traffic quantity.

nodes.label: Unit Economics as North Star for Franchising
nodes.description: **Framework: Unit Economics as North Star for Franchising** — Every franchise-demand problem traces back to a single root cause: the unit economics of each individual restaurant. Fix per-location profitability first; franchise interest is a downstream symptom.

nodes.label: Four-Part Profit Optimization Sequence
nodes.description: **Framework: Four-Part Profit Optimization Sequence** — A sequential four-step plan to triple EBITDA without growing revenue: (1) fix the sales motion, (2) optimize pricing and packaging per service line, (3) generate sufficient cash flow, (4) acquire the talent needed to shore up infrastructure.

nodes.label: Cloud-to-Dirt Knowledge Stack
nodes.description: **Framework: Cloud-to-Dirt Knowledge Stack** — Vertical integration of knowledge from high-level strategy and people management down to granular API-level technical execution; enables a business owner to see cross-functional AI applications that pure technologists cannot.

nodes.label: AI as Tool, Not Business
nodes.description: **Framework: AI as Tool, Not Business** — Businesses should use AI as one of many operational tools (analogous to the internet) rather than repositioning themselves as AI companies; the goal is better outcomes, not AI as identity.

nodes.label: Barbell AI Strategy
nodes.description: **Framework: Barbell AI Strategy** — Position on two extremes simultaneously: high-risk AI-first operations on one pole, and bets on timeless human needs (health, food, entertainment) on the other; avoid the unprotected middle.

nodes.label: Workflow-First Org Design
