nodes.description: **Framework: Workflow-First Org Design** — Replace role-based org thinking with workflow-based thinking: decompose every role into four to ten granular tasks, then ask which tasks can live inside an automated workflow instead of headcount.

nodes.label: BYOS / BYOA Model
nodes.description: **Framework: BYOS / BYOA Model** — Bring Your Own Software or Bring Your Own Agent: employees and contractors who arrive with pre-built AI agents that replace entire department outputs become disproportionately valuable as labor markets shift.

nodes.label: Five-Stage Script Rotation
nodes.plugin: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence
nodes.description: **Framework: Five-Stage Script Rotation** — A weekly cycle of daily role-play sessions covering five discrete script stages: intro, discovery, offer, objections/looping, and a rotating hot-topic day based on team need.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence
nodes.topic: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

nodes.label: Three-Bucket Avatar Segmentation
nodes.description: **Framework: Three-Bucket Avatar Segmentation** — Segment prospects into three classification buckets before selling: demographics (who they look like), quantifiables (business size, revenue), and behaviors (actions taken by activated vs. churned look-alikes).

nodes.label: Elephant and Rider Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Elephant and Rider Model** — Dual model of the brain in which the conscious mind (rider) sits atop the subconscious mind (elephant); the rider cannot force the elephant to do anything it does not want to do.

nodes.label: Rider-Elephant Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Rider-Elephant Model** — A mental model dividing human decision-making into the rational rider (which generates reasons and justifications) and the emotional elephant (which generates emotions and determines actual behavior through instinctive responses).

nodes.label: Post-Rationalization Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Post-Rationalization Model** — The brain constructs plausible-sounding justifications for decisions already made instinctively; conscious reasoning acts as post-hoc narrative building rather than actual decision mechanism.

nodes.label: Uncertainty and Delay as Upside Filter
nodes.description: **Framework: Uncertainty and Delay as Upside Filter** — All the upside worth having in life sits behind exactly two prices people refuse to pay: uncertainty (not knowing the outcome) and delay (not knowing how long to wait). Because most people are unwilling to bear these two costs, they remain the primary arbitrage opportunities.

nodes.label: Trial-to-Activation Rebate Structure
nodes.description: **Framework: Trial-to-Activation Rebate Structure** — Two-step activation incentive: charge upfront, then rebate or waive the next billing period if the user completes a defined first-value action within the trial window.

nodes.label: 40-for-2 Management Trade
nodes.description: **Framework: 40-for-2 Management Trade** — A founder trades 40 hours of direct selling for 2 hours of managing a salesperson; repeating this trade accumulates until the founder does 40 hours of management and zero selling, then can trade management hours to a manager in turn.

nodes.label: Free Trial Plus Penalty Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Free Trial Plus Penalty Model** — A client-acquisition model where prospects receive service at no charge in exchange for behaving as required; failure to complete specified behaviors triggers a billing event. Designed to fill a proof pipeline when testimonials are absent.

nodes.label: Two End-States Framework for Client-Acquisition Agencies
nodes.description: **Framework: Two End-States Framework for Client-Acquisition Agencies** — Client-acquisition agencies for small businesses inevitably converge on one of two viable long-run business models: ultra-low-cost high-volume automation or high-ticket whale/upmarket positioning. The mid-market is structurally unviable.

nodes.label: Click-to-Close Vertical Integration
nodes.plugin: Vertical Integration to Capture Full Margin
nodes.description: **Framework: Click-to-Close Vertical Integration** — The strategic goal of owning every stage of the deal pipeline from lead sourcing through close, eliminating external gatekeepers and capturing full margin at each stage.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Vertical Integration to Capture Full Margin
nodes.topic: Vertical Integration to Capture Full Margin

nodes.label: Defend the Perimeter Metaphor
nodes.description: **Framework: Defend the Perimeter Metaphor** — A spatial analogy comparing business focus to a single soldier guarding progressively larger areas: one room (easy), one building (hard), one block (nearly impossible) — illustrating that spreading attention across multiple business lines is like a single defender guarding an entire city block alone.

nodes.label: Moral High Ground Delivery Change Pitch
nodes.description: **Framework: Moral High Ground Delivery Change Pitch** — A reframing technique for announcing service delivery reductions: position the change as fulfilling a prior promise (integrity), enumerate reasons it benefits clients, and make any objection equivalent to attacking your integrity.

nodes.label: Want Less or Trade More
nodes.description: **Framework: Want Less or Trade More** — A two-option resolution to the dissatisfaction of wanting two incompatible things: either reduce your desire for the thing you say you want, or pay the cost required to get it. There is no third path.

nodes.label: Active Active, Passive Passive
nodes.description: **Framework: Active Active, Passive Passive** — A capital management rule: keep passive investments managed by partners so they consume no founder attention, and deploy active effort only in the core business where ROI on time is highest.

nodes.label: Three Value-Creation Frames for Premium Offers
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Value-Creation Frames for Premium Offers** — Three intellectual attack vectors for designing a premium one-on-one offer: (1) 10x/100x price thought-experiment to identify low-cost high-value inclusions; (2) word-of-mouth-only constraint to identify what a perfect customer experience requires; (3) remove-unscalable-but-keep-10x-value to engineer a scalable high-value tier.

nodes.label: Premium Tier Anchor Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Premium Tier Anchor Model** — A two-tier offer structure where an expensive unscalable one-on-one tier is listed alongside a scalable lower-priced tier; the premium tier anchors perceived value for the scalable tier via price contrast and brand narrative even if few or no premium buyers convert.

nodes.label: SPCL Influence Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: SPCL Influence Framework** — Four stacked components that determine a creator's influence over an audience: Status (controls scarce resources), Power (say-do correspondence reinforcement history), Credibility (third-party verifiable proof), Likeness (demographic or values similarity).

nodes.label: Proof-Promise-Plan Introduction Structure
nodes.description: **Framework: Proof-Promise-Plan Introduction Structure** — A three-part educational video introduction: Proof (demonstrate you can do what you claim), Promise (state what the viewer will get or learn), Plan (set expectations for what happens next). Order is flexible; lead with whichever element matters most for the specific content.

nodes.label: Four Audience Monetization Paths
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Audience Monetization Paths** — Four ways to monetize an existing audience arranged on a continuum from low-risk/low-value to high-risk/high-value: (1) Affiliates — paid after sales on standard terms; (2) Sponsorships — paid upfront as a traffic source via CPM or whitelisting; (3) Partnerships — equity deals ranging from minority to majority; (4) Own brand — start your own product from scratch.

nodes.label: Bouquet Brand Assembly Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Bouquet Brand Assembly Model** — A brand is built by deliberately pairing your product or name with people, experiences, and values your ideal customer already likes. Each pairing is a flower; repeated positive pairings form a bouquet (the brand). Narrowing means clustering similar flowers; expanding means adding adjacent ones. A single bad pairing is one rotten flower that mars the whole bouquet.

nodes.label: Six-Step First $100K Roadmap
nodes.description: **Framework: Six-Step First $100K Roadmap** — A sequential six-step plan to earn and bank $100K: (1) cut all costs, (2) save time, (3) research skills people already pay for, (4) spend time learning through iteration, (5) spend money on tools/implementation/attempts, (6) do not increase lifestyle.

nodes.label: 4-4-4 Time Split
nodes.description: **Framework: 4-4-4 Time Split** — For people without a 9-to-5 job, divide 12 active hours into three four-hour blocks: promotion (letting people know about your offer), delivery (fulfilling what you promised), and building (researching opportunities and prioritizing next actions).

nodes.label: First-Party Data Learning Loop
nodes.description: **Framework: First-Party Data Learning Loop** — A five-step skill-acquisition cycle: (1) do high volume, (2) analyze the top 10% of outputs, (3) identify what differentiates the top 10% from the bottom 90%, (4) isolate the most important variable, (5) avoid the mistakes the bottom 90% keeps making, then repeat 100 more times.

nodes.label: 1-1-1 Rule
nodes.description: **Framework: 1-1-1 Rule** — Sell one product or service to one avatar on one channel until you reach $1 million in revenue; do not diversify until that milestone is hit.

nodes.label: Trim and Stack Offer Design
nodes.description: **Framework: Trim and Stack Offer Design** — A two-phase offer redesign process: first list all current deliverables, then cut and recombine them to retain only what clients most value, eliminating everything else to reduce delivery load while maintaining perceived value.

nodes.label: Supply Constraint Resolution Matrix
nodes.description: **Framework: Supply Constraint Resolution Matrix** — Four-lever framework for resolving capacity bottlenecks in service businesses: (1) raise price so fewer people buy, (2) change delivery ratio from 1:1 to 1:N, (3) productize the delivery, or (4) hire additional staff to absorb load.

nodes.label: SCARF Model (Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, Fairness)
nodes.description: **Framework: SCARF Model (Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, Fairness)** — Five psychological dimensions (Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, Fairness) that humans care about deeply and that economists systematically ignore; boosting any one of these drives adoption, satisfaction, or behavior change independent of the product's functional attributes.

nodes.label: Messaging vs. Signaling Distinction
nodes.description: **Framework: Messaging vs. Signaling Distinction** — Two fundamentally different communication modes: Messaging (efficient information transfer when sender is trusted) and Signaling (costly, broadcast communication that functions as proof of sincerity and quality when trust is absent). Optimizing for messaging efficiency in a signaling context destroys trust.

nodes.label: Psycho-logic / Alchemy of Second-Order Sense
nodes.description: **Framework: Psycho-logic / Alchemy of Second-Order Sense** — A design philosophy that looks for solutions in non-obvious psychological dimensions rather than logical-functional ones; the best innovations make second-order sense (they work through perception, status, context-framing) rather than first-order logical sense, because first-order solutions are already competed away.

nodes.label: Systemic vs. Segment Market Diagnosis
nodes.description: **Framework: Systemic vs. Segment Market Diagnosis** — Before committing to a business model pivot, determine whether the revenue decline is systemic (affecting all carriers/markets nationwide) or segment-specific (one state or carrier class); only a systemic verdict justifies model-level change.

nodes.label: Back-End Continuity Test
nodes.description: **Framework: Back-End Continuity Test** — Before replacing a transactional model with a subscription model, first test whether existing emergency/transactional customers can be converted to a recurring offer at point of service completion; inability to close that upsell is decisive evidence against switching the entire model.

nodes.label: Passion Etymology Reframe
nodes.description: **Framework: Passion Etymology Reframe** — Reframes passion from doing what you love to finding something meaningful enough to suffer for, rooted in the Latin root passio (suffering) and its first usage in the Passion of Christ.

nodes.label: Fixed-Cost Suffering Model
nodes.plugin: All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice
nodes.description: **Framework: Fixed-Cost Suffering Model** — All life paths (employment, entrepreneurship, wealth, poverty, marriage, singlehood) carry equivalent suffering; the variable is what you receive in return, not whether you suffer.
nodes.parent_id: concept:All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice
nodes.topic: All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice

nodes.label: Return on Capital Optimization
nodes.description: **Framework: Return on Capital Optimization** — Evaluate every business model variant by return on human capital and financial capital, not by absolute revenue or profit, to identify which format to scale.

nodes.label: Split-the-Difference Roll-Up Offer
nodes.description: **Framework: Split-the-Difference Roll-Up Offer** — A two-stage multiple structure for DSO consolidation: offer practice owners their solo-sale multiple (4x) plus a share of the uplift to the consolidated multiple (7x), keeping everything above 7x as the consolidator's profit.

nodes.label: Coaching Business as the Goose
nodes.description: **Framework: Coaching Business as the Goose** — Retain the educational/coaching business as the permanent demand-generation asset (the goose) while selling the consolidated practice group (the eggs); the coaching book supplies a continual pipeline of willing consolidation targets.

nodes.label: First Impression Anchoring Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: First Impression Anchoring Framework** — Initial decisions and impressions on a stimulus (like checking into a hotel) anchor all subsequent perceptions of that same stimulus, with evidence-seeking behavior reinforcing the initial judgment.

nodes.label: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem Definition
nodes.description: **Framework: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem Definition** — A three-question framework for defining business problems: What does it mean? How do you know that? Why do you care? Forces quantitative grounding of vague claims.

nodes.label: Fast Cash Play via Existing Resources
nodes.description: **Framework: Fast Cash Play via Existing Resources** — A structured approach to generating immediate client revenue by mobilizing the client's existing dead contacts, old customers, or social media audience before new acquisition begins, making the product self-funding within 30 days.

nodes.label: Win Your Money Back Dual-Conversion Frame
nodes.description: **Framework: Win Your Money Back Dual-Conversion Frame** — A $500 front-end offer where the customer earns a 100% store credit by completing daily habits (activation) and submitting multi-platform testimonials (referral), with the store credit rolling into a full-year upsell at $5,000; combines results guarantee with social proof harvest in one mechanism.

nodes.label: Court Filter for Observable Language
nodes.description: **Framework: Court Filter for Observable Language** — A translation discipline requiring all marketing and sales copy to describe only observable, court-admissible behaviors — physical actions, visible states, measurable outputs — removing interpretive or amorphous language that cannot be verified by a third party.

nodes.label: Evolution as Advertising-Driven Process
nodes.description: **Framework: Evolution as Advertising-Driven Process** — Much of evolutionary progress is driven by the need to attract mates through costly signals; these signals function as natural advertising campaigns that drive behavioral selection.

nodes.label: Four Components of Equity Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Components of Equity Framework** — A decomposition of what real equity provides into four distinct elements — cash flow, sale bonus, risk, and control — used to identify which elements a prospective equity recipient actually wants, then substitute non-dilutive instruments for those elements only.

nodes.label: Profit Share Pool Structure
nodes.description: **Framework: Profit Share Pool Structure** — A fixed percentage of annual profit (typically 10–20%) set aside as a leadership incentive pool; individual leaders receive slices of that pool rather than ownership stakes, capping total incentive spend while creating owner-like thinking.

nodes.label: Scientific Attribution Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Scientific Attribution Model** — A blended attribution rule: if a conversion occurs within 30 days of a touchpoint, assign credit to the last touch; if the gap exceeds 30 days, assign credit to the first touch. This prevents both the short-termism of pure last-touch and the brand-inflation of pure first-touch.

nodes.label: Sales Hire Pattern Recognition Ladder
nodes.description: **Framework: Sales Hire Pattern Recognition Ladder** — Founders must fail-and-learn through each successive sales hire type (SDR, salesperson, manager, closer, director, VP) in sequence; pattern recognition for what good looks like only comes after multiple failures at each level.

nodes.label: Investor Risk Ladder
nodes.description: **Framework: Investor Risk Ladder** — Investors pay down assumptions, not ideas; each funding round represents a specific assumption that was de-risked, and the valuation step-up must be justified by naming which assumption was proved true.

nodes.label: Find-Sell-Deliver Sequence
nodes.description: **Framework: Find-Sell-Deliver Sequence** — When launching a new product or service, identify a customer first, sell them on a meaningful outcome you will deliver, and commit to staying until they are satisfied — before building a detailed plan or process.

nodes.label: Evidence-Over-Emotion Self-Assessment
nodes.description: **Framework: Evidence-Over-Emotion Self-Assessment** — Apply the same evidence standard you use to judge others when evaluating your own character traits; a trait is possessed if observable behavior demonstrates it, regardless of whether you feel you have it.

nodes.label: Penny-on-the-Scale Accumulation
nodes.description: **Framework: Penny-on-the-Scale Accumulation** — Build a character trait by accumulating undeniable behavioral proof one action at a time; each act consistent with the trait adds a penny to the scale until the weight of evidence makes the self-attribution credible.

nodes.label: Ratchet Effect
nodes.plugin: Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP
nodes.description: **Framework: Ratchet Effect** — A class of products and technologies where adoption is very slow until a threshold of experience is crossed, after which reversion is near-zero; the value of the product is only revealed through use, not through prior reasoning.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP
nodes.topic: Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP

nodes.label: EAST Behavioral Adoption Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: EAST Behavioral Adoption Framework** — A four-lever framework for accelerating behavior adoption: make the target behavior Easy, Attractive, Social, and Timely. Rory Sutherland applies it specifically to recycling and sustainable product adoption.

nodes.label: Map vs. Territory (Korzybski Applied to Economics)
nodes.plugin: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking
nodes.description: **Framework: Map vs. Territory (Korzybski Applied to Economics)** — Economics provides a map of human behavior; reality is the territory. What the economic map omits (context, packaging, psychological association) is often more important than what the map contains. Coined by Alfred Korzybski; applied here to consumer valuation by Rory Sutherland.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking
nodes.topic: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking

nodes.label: Operational vs. Psychological Value Creation
nodes.description: **Framework: Operational vs. Psychological Value Creation** — Two distinct value-creation modes: operational (process efficiency, cost reduction, widely pursued, subject to diminishing returns) and psychological (context, packaging, association, perception — largely ignored by CEOs/CFOs because it is non-numerical and uncertain). Rory Sutherland argues the second mode has orders-of-magnitude greater untapped potential.

nodes.label: Three-Lever Scaling Sequence
nodes.description: **Framework: Three-Lever Scaling Sequence** — Fix sales motion first, then raise prices, then use increased profit to improve talent retention — each lever unlocks the next.

nodes.label: Expanded Career Ladder Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Expanded Career Ladder Framework** — Transform a 3-rung career path into 9-18 rungs by subdividing each existing title into junior, normal, and senior tiers, alternating title upgrades with tangible perks so employees are always 3-6 months from the next promotion.

nodes.label: Debt Risk Quantification Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Debt Risk Quantification Framework** — A three-variable coverage-ratio analysis (seasonal volatility, cash flow vs. debt covenants, and coverage buffer) that converts emotional debt fear into a tractable math problem.

nodes.label: Partnership Justification Test
nodes.description: **Framework: Partnership Justification Test** — A partnership only creates value if the partner supplies something the other party genuinely lacks: money, time, skills, or network/distribution. Absence of at least one gap means one partner is redundant.

nodes.label: Drop Low or Go High
nodes.description: **Framework: Drop Low or Go High** — Digital marketing agencies serving SMBs must choose between two viable poles: ultra-cheap automated delivery (≤$400/month) or high-touch services for sophisticated business owners with proven metrics; the middle band ($1,500–$3,000/month) is a structural dead zone.

nodes.label: Launch and Integrate Affiliate Strategy
nodes.description: **Framework: Launch and Integrate Affiliate Strategy** — Two-step process for activating affiliate partners: a launch (get a batch of referrals fast to create an internal case study) followed by integration (embedding your service into the affiliate's standard onboarding so every new client they bring on automatically becomes your client).

nodes.label: Data as Rationality Signaling
nodes.description: **Framework: Data as Rationality Signaling** — In modern business culture, the display of numerical data serves as a social signal of rationality and credibility, regardless of data quality.

nodes.label: Three-Level AI Service Delivery Stack
nodes.description: **Framework: Three-Level AI Service Delivery Stack** — A progression from websites (level 1) to individual automations (level 2) to full integrated AI systems (level 3), where each level requires more skill and commands higher prices.

nodes.label: Doctor Sales Approach
nodes.description: **Framework: Doctor Sales Approach** — A consultative sales structure where the seller talks 20% of the time and asks diagnostic questions that lead the prospect to identify their own pain, then positions the seller's service as the solution.

nodes.label: Five-Step AI Business Roadmap
nodes.description: **Framework: Five-Step AI Business Roadmap** — A sequenced roadmap from (1) learn a skill, (2) work for free to build proof, (3) sustain yourself ($2-3k/month), (4) charge more and filter clients, to (5) identify and solve bottlenecks continuously.

nodes.label: Result-Based vs Upfront-Plus-Recurring Pricing
nodes.description: **Framework: Result-Based vs Upfront-Plus-Recurring Pricing** — Two primary pricing structures for AI services: (1) result-based at 20% of gross profit generated, which pays more when work is excellent but requires trackability; (2) upfront setup fee plus monthly recurring, used when results are hard to attribute, combined with a satisfaction guarantee.

nodes.label: Face-Saving Re-Entry Frame
nodes.plugin: Partnership Equity Must Be Codified Upfront
nodes.description: **Framework: Face-Saving Re-Entry Frame** — A negotiation tactic for allowing a previously resistant partner to accept new terms without humiliation by reframing their earlier refusal as contextually reasonable and shifting blame to external demand pressure.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Partnership Equity Must Be Codified Upfront
nodes.topic: Partnership Equity Must Be Codified Upfront

nodes.label: Replace-Six Strategy
nodes.description: **Framework: Replace-Six Strategy** — Rather than scaling headcount of low-quality clients, replace current clients one-for-one with higher-quality, compliant clients over a 12-month horizon, then go deep on the single best performer.

nodes.label: Sell to the Rich, Not From Your Own Wallet
nodes.description: **Framework: Sell to the Rich, Not From Your Own Wallet** — A pricing mindset framework asserting that entrepreneurs should price for the top 10% wealth tier (net worth $1M+), not for the 50th-percentile buyer who is never their customer.

nodes.label: LTV-Conversion Rate Model Selection Test
nodes.description: **Framework: LTV-Conversion Rate Model Selection Test** — Compare two business models by asking three questions: (1) Does more of the target market want it (conversion rate)? (2) Is the lifetime gross profit per customer higher? (3) Is the CAC comparable or lower? The model that wins on all three is mathematically superior.

nodes.label: Build for Cold, Works Everywhere
nodes.plugin: Warm vs. Cold Sales Process Mismatch
nodes.description: **Framework: Build for Cold, Works Everywhere** — A sales process designed for cold (unwarmed) leads will function on warm leads too; a warm-only process underconverts cold traffic by a large margin.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Warm vs. Cold Sales Process Mismatch
nodes.topic: Warm vs. Cold Sales Process Mismatch

nodes.label: Cold-Lead Sales Architecture (VSL + Qualification + Training Cadence)
nodes.description: **Framework: Cold-Lead Sales Architecture (VSL + Qualification + Training Cadence)** — Three-component system for cold traffic: (1) video sales letter pre-frames and filters before the call, (2) structured qualification gates separate genuinely qualified prospects, (3) ongoing sales training cadence ensures reps follow the process consistently.

nodes.label: Dawn to Dusk Portfolio
nodes.description: **Framework: Dawn to Dusk Portfolio** — A brand portfolio organized to cover every meal occasion from morning to evening, enabling cross-category household penetration without a single brand bearing all positioning weight.

nodes.label: Become a Friend Programme (Ella's Kitchen)
nodes.description: **Framework: Become a Friend Programme (Ella's Kitchen)** — A post-purchase loyalty and education programme for parents of Ella's Kitchen customers, combining weaning guides, feeding resources, and direct customer care contact to function as a trusted advisor rather than a brand.

nodes.label: Today Constraint vs. Horizon Constraint
nodes.description: **Framework: Today Constraint vs. Horizon Constraint** — Distinguish the constraint blocking growth right now (sales/marketing) from the constraint that will become existential at a future date (facility/supply); address today's constraint first unless the horizon constraint's timeline forces earlier action.

nodes.label: Launch Then Integrate B2B Partnership Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Launch Then Integrate B2B Partnership Model** — Enter a B2B partner relationship with a one-time co-webinar launch to build goodwill, then transition to permanent integration into the partner's sales motion so the partner sells the complementary service as a standard add-on.

nodes.label: Three Content Buckets
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Content Buckets** — A taxonomy dividing all content into entertainment (goal: get people to watch), education (goal: change behavior), and edutainment (goal: both simultaneously); the prevailing outcome across viewers determines the bucket.

nodes.label: Proof-Promise-Plan Introduction Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Proof-Promise-Plan Introduction Framework** — A three-element intro structure for educational videos: Proof (evidence you can deliver on the promise), Promise (what the viewer will gain), and Plan (the steps that will get them there); order is flexible — lead with whichever element is most important for the content.

nodes.label: Four Paths to Mega Money
nodes.description: **Framework: Four Paths to Mega Money** — A 2x2 framework combining your money vs. other people's money with your business vs. other people's businesses to produce four distinct wealth-building paths: bootstrapping, raising capital, investing, and fund management.

nodes.label: The Going Pro Decision
nodes.description: **Framework: The Going Pro Decision** — A binary internal commitment to pursue a skill or goal at a professional standard, triggered by a deliberate choice rather than external circumstances, with the understanding that effort will never receive credit and that the work must be done purely for the doer.

nodes.label: Six Levels of Making Money
nodes.description: **Framework: Six Levels of Making Money** — A ranked hierarchy of six compensation structures ordered by leverage and risk transfer: (1) work then get paid, (2) pay as you go, (3) pay then work, (4) when X happens you pay me, (5) sell/buy risk itself (insurance model), (6) no-matter-what you pay me (government/monopoly model).

nodes.label: Behavioral Trauma Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Behavioral Trauma Framework** — A two-axis diagnostic: (1) was there a permanent behavior change from an aversive stimulus? — determines whether trauma occurred; (2) does the behavior change move toward or away from long-term goals? — determines whether the outcome was positive or negative.

nodes.label: Performance-Based Zero-Capital Business Selection
nodes.description: **Framework: Performance-Based Zero-Capital Business Selection** — Two criteria for selecting a business when starting with zero capital: (1) pay-for-performance compensation structure so no capital is required to start earning, and (2) no upfront cost to operate, meaning the business runs on the founder's time and skill rather than inventory or ad spend.

nodes.label: Vendor Discount Arbitrage Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Vendor Discount Arbitrage Model** — Negotiate a discounted bulk rate from a business owner (the delivery cost floor), then sell to end customers at a higher market price; the spread between the two prices is the founder's margin, requiring zero capital if the business owner absorbs delivery cost.

nodes.label: Behavioral vs. Attitudinal Data Hierarchy
nodes.description: **Framework: Behavioral vs. Attitudinal Data Hierarchy** — Behavioral data (what people actually do) is more valuable and revealing than attitudinal data (what people claim they do), because self-reported intentions systematically diverge from revealed preferences.

nodes.label: Ergodicity Fallacy in Aggregate Statistics
nodes.description: **Framework: Ergodicity Fallacy in Aggregate Statistics** — The false assumption that what is good on average for a population doing something once is also good for a single individual doing the same thing repeatedly; this misapplication of ensemble averages to time-series decisions produces fatally wrong conclusions in economics, policy, and risk.

nodes.label: Scale Zero Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Scale Zero Framework** — A principle requiring the founder to reduce their personal operational contribution to zero before a business can scale without ceiling; any function requiring founder involvement caps total scale.

nodes.label: Two Service Business Reinvestment Paths
nodes.description: **Framework: Two Service Business Reinvestment Paths** — Service businesses should direct end-of-year profit into exactly two categories: A-player talent acquisition or brand-building plays (high-visibility associations), not physical capital or general overhead.

nodes.label: Explore-Exploit Trade-off
nodes.description: **Framework: Explore-Exploit Trade-off** — Every surviving organization must balance exploiting known information (reliable, short-term return) with exploring for unknown or new information (costly in the short term but essential for adaptation and survival). The ratio between the two is a strategic choice with survival consequences.

nodes.label: Waggle Dance Incentive Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Waggle Dance Incentive Model** — Rory Sutherland's framing of how bee colonies solve information-sharing incentives: explore-bees share new discoveries with the hive; the length of the waggle dance is proportionate to the significance of the find, creating a natural reward signal for information sharing that most human organizations lack.

nodes.label: Ergodicity Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Ergodicity Framework** — The distinction between ensemble average (many people taking a bet once) and time average (one person taking the same bet repeatedly). A bet that is profitable on average for a group can still be ruinous for individuals because the majority can end up poorer than their starting position even while the group average rises.

nodes.label: Innovation Adoption Gap
nodes.description: **Framework: Innovation Adoption Gap** — The gap between technological invention and market adoption is a function of perception and marketing, not product quality; historical hindsight compresses this gap into apparent instantaneity.

nodes.label: Marketing Moonshot Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Marketing Moonshot Framework** — A two-category model separating standard-optimization activity (80% of bees following the waggle dance) from exploratory high-variance bets (20% rogue bees) where failure is frequent but rare successes pay back 10,000-fold; applied to marketing as changing perception rather than physical reality to achieve order-of-magnitude improvements at relatively low cost.

nodes.label: Satisficing vs. Optimizing Decision Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Satisficing vs. Optimizing Decision Model** — Herbert Simon's distinction between archery-style optimization (aim for the single best outcome) and darts-style satisficing (aim for the southwestern quadrant to avoid catastrophic low scores); in evolutionary and business contexts, satisficing considers both average outcome and worst-case variance, not only the maximum.

nodes.label: Costly Signaling / Handicap Theory
nodes.description: **Framework: Costly Signaling / Handicap Theory** — Amotz Zahavi's principle that meaningful signals require genuine cost (financial, effort, time, creativity) because cheap signals are unreliable; applied to marketing, advertising spend, gift-giving, and brand behavior as mechanisms that signal long-term commitment and trustworthiness to observers.

nodes.label: Five AI Workers System
nodes.description: **Framework: Five AI Workers System** — A bundled agency offer of five AI-driven automation roles — outreach specialist (database reactivation), reputation manager (reviews and referrals), website lead nurturing, AI receptionist (missed call text-back), and marketing director (paid ads with AI lead nurturing) — sold together to local businesses as an inseparable department rather than individual point solutions.

nodes.label: Niche Research Rubric
nodes.plugin: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting
nodes.description: **Framework: Niche Research Rubric** — A four-criteria filter for selecting an agency niche: proof of concept (other agencies succeeding), total addressable market over 10,000 businesses, high-ticket recurring pricing, and a growing market; evaluated via Claude prompt.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting
nodes.topic: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

nodes.label: The Lonely Chapter
nodes.description: **Framework: The Lonely Chapter** — The early phase of an exceptional path during which the founder operates without peer support, social validation, or external cheering — positioned as a diagnostic signal that you are on the right path rather than a problem to solve.

nodes.label: Protect Your Passion
nodes.description: **Framework: Protect Your Passion** — A discipline of actively preserving enthusiasm for one's work during the low-reward early phase, because passion destroyed before compounding kicks in inverts the effort-reward relationship at precisely the time when effort has the highest return.

nodes.label: Epic Story Razor
nodes.description: **Framework: Epic Story Razor** — A personal decision heuristic: when choosing between paths, default to whichever option produces the most compelling long-arc narrative, on the reasoning that the most epic story is almost never the shortest path to victory.

nodes.label: Map-Territory Distinction
nodes.description: **Framework: Map-Territory Distinction** — Economic models (maps) abstract from reality (territory); the information omitted from the model is often more important than what the model contains.

nodes.label: Close Rate to Price Multiple Ladder
nodes.description: **Framework: Close Rate to Price Multiple Ladder** — A tiered rule-of-thumb mapping sales close rates to implied pricing multiples, used to diagnose whether a business is underpriced relative to demand.

nodes.label: LTV:CAC Human-in-Loop Multiplier
nodes.description: **Framework: LTV:CAC Human-in-Loop Multiplier** — A framework for setting minimum LTV-to-CAC ratio targets based on how many of three business functions (attraction, conversion, delivery) involve a human, scaling from 3:1 (all automated) to 12:1 (all human).

nodes.label: 30-Day Cash Collected Rule
nodes.description: **Framework: 30-Day Cash Collected Rule** — A cash-flow rule requiring that gross profit collected within the first 30 days of a new customer relationship exceeds the sum of CAC plus COGS, enabling a self-funding acquisition loop.

nodes.label: Darwinian Costly Signalling Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Darwinian Costly Signalling Framework** — Signalling only carries information when it is costly (in resources or difficulty); low-cost signals are ignored or discounted by receivers because they cannot distinguish fit from unfit.

nodes.label: Guppy Three-Stage Mate-Selection Heuristic
nodes.description: **Framework: Guppy Three-Stage Mate-Selection Heuristic** — Female guppies apply a three-stage decision tree: (1) choose the 50%-larger male by size; (2) if sizes are close, choose the more-orange male; (3) if coloring is similar, apply social proof and choose the male observed mating with a peer.

nodes.label: Clouds-and-Clocks Spectrum
nodes.description: **Framework: Clouds-and-Clocks Spectrum** — Karl Popper's taxonomy positioning phenomena on a spectrum from clouds (complex, emergent, unpredictable: markets, ecosystems) to clocks (mechanistic, mathematically modelable: bridges, engines); the gravest intellectual error is treating clouds as clocks.

nodes.label: School Bias Toward False Rationality
nodes.description: **Framework: School Bias Toward False Rationality** — Educational systems teach two apparently distinct subject categories—exact sciences (maths, physics, chemistry) with apparent single answers, and arts with inherent ambiguity—creating a false perception that rationality requires mathematical models with provably single answers.

nodes.label: Creator Risk Continuum
nodes.description: **Framework: Creator Risk Continuum** — A spectrum from low-risk to high-risk creator types (entertainer -> B2C educator -> B2B prosumer -> B2B expert) where risk is defined by the potential downside to the consumer of acting on the advice; AI disrupts low-risk types first and high-risk types last.

nodes.label: Self-Linking Business Loop
nodes.description: **Framework: Self-Linking Business Loop** — An engineered business motion in which the delivery of the core product or service generates marketing proof automatically, which in turn acquires more customers, creating a compounding self-reinforcing cycle.

nodes.label: Always Invert Framework
nodes.plugin: Contrarian Conviction as Outsized Return Driver
nodes.description: **Framework: Always Invert Framework** — A decision discipline attributed by Rory Sutherland to Charlie Munger: for any dominant assumption, actively construct and test the opposite hypothesis before accepting the consensus view.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Contrarian Conviction as Outsized Return Driver
nodes.topic: Contrarian Conviction as Outsized Return Driver

nodes.label: Physical Fallacy
nodes.description: **Framework: Physical Fallacy** — A cognitive bias named by Steven Pinker in which people systematically assign lower value to intangible goods and services than to physical ones, even when the intangible creates equivalent or greater utility.

nodes.label: Anti-Fragility Economic Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Anti-Fragility Economic Model** — Nassim Taleb's framework arguing that complex systems including economies are strengthened by frequent mild stressors; suppressing those stressors creates fragility and eventual catastrophic failure.

nodes.label: Discount Plus One-Time Fee Structure
nodes.description: **Framework: Discount Plus One-Time Fee Structure** — A two-part offer that charges a deeply discounted first term to lower acquisition friction, then adds one or more separately named one-time fees to fund commissions and reduce churn.

nodes.label: Four-Step One-Time Fee Creation
nodes.description: **Framework: Four-Step One-Time Fee Creation** — A four-step process to create any made-up fee: (1) pick fee name, (2) pick fee price, (3) pick reason why, (4) start charging, discounting, or waiving it.

nodes.label: Newtonian Physics vs. Human Perception Frame
nodes.description: **Framework: Newtonian Physics vs. Human Perception Frame** — The erroneous assumption that humans respond to objective, measurable reality causes a monumental misdirection of effort in design and marketing; the correct frame is that humans respond to perceived, contextual, and emotional reality — not physical metrics.

nodes.label: Sonic Identity as Brand Property
nodes.description: **Framework: Sonic Identity as Brand Property** — A named musical or jingle identity functions as a superpower brand property with measurable recognition, familiarity, and reassurance value — distinct from and often outperforming verbal or visual brand assets.

nodes.label: Occasion-Driven Price Perception
nodes.description: **Framework: Occasion-Driven Price Perception** — The value customers perceive in a purchase depends on the significance of the occasion, not the product's intrinsic properties; occasion context justifies premium pricing that would appear unreasonable in ordinary contexts.

nodes.label: Pareto Pricing Tier Framework
nodes.plugin: Pareto Pricing: Four-Tier Structure at 5-10x Gaps
nodes.description: **Framework: Pareto Pricing Tier Framework** — Four price tiers with 5-10x gaps between each level; expect approximately 20% of customers at each tier to take the next step up; top tiers generate the majority of profit despite minority of customers.
nodes.topic: Pareto Pricing: Four-Tier Structure at 5-10x Gaps

nodes.label: Rider and Elephant (Haidt)
nodes.description: **Framework: Rider and Elephant (Haidt)** — Jonathan Haidt's metaphor: the elephant is System 1 (instinctive, habitual, non-verbal), the rider is System 2 (conscious, rational, verbal). The rider believes he controls the elephant but mostly post-rationalizes what the elephant has already decided; the rider is the Press Office, not the Oval Office.

nodes.label: Acquisition Utility vs Transaction Utility (Thaler)
nodes.description: **Framework: Acquisition Utility vs Transaction Utility (Thaler)** — Richard Thaler's two-component model of purchase psychology: acquisition utility is the subjective value of owning or consuming the thing; transaction utility is the emotional quality of the purchase act itself (fairness, guilt, pleasure). A product can have high acquisition utility but low transaction utility, explaining why people want things they feel unable to buy.

nodes.label: Defensive Decision-Making (Minimax)
nodes.description: **Framework: Defensive Decision-Making (Minimax)** — A decision bias in which individuals unconsciously choose options that minimize worst-case personal embarrassment rather than maximize expected value. The operative question is not 'what is the best outcome?' but 'in the worst case, to what extent will I look like an idiot?' Leads to systematic over-reliance on defaults.

nodes.label: Replace-Not-Scale Partner Sequencing
nodes.description: **Framework: Replace-Not-Scale Partner Sequencing** — When a partner portfolio has low-quality or legally gray clients, the path to growth is replacing the six existing clients with six higher-quality ones before attempting volume expansion.

nodes.label: R&D Distribution Model
nodes.description: **Framework: R&D Distribution Model** — A monthly R&D process where the operator selects 10-20 representative accounts from the distribution base, assigns a fixed budget to test one pressing problem, and releases results to the full base monthly regardless of outcome.

nodes.label: Must Be Easy Diagnostic
nodes.description: **Framework: Must Be Easy Diagnostic** — The phrase 'it must be easy' is a reliable surface signal of victim-mindset; its presence indicates the speaker is externalizing inadequacy onto circumstances rather than accepting agency.

nodes.label: Eleven Rules of Profitable Irrationality
nodes.description: **Framework: Eleven Rules of Profitable Irrationality** — A structured set of eleven principles (with invited extension) for generating competitive advantage by being less logical than competitors, covering contrarian logic, system complexity, psychological reframing, and empirical experimentation.

nodes.label: Adaptive Preference Formation
nodes.description: **Framework: Adaptive Preference Formation** — A psychological mechanism by which people forced to choose option A over B construct a narrative in which they prefer A anyway, minimizing regret — exploitable in product and choice architecture design to manufacture net utility from nothing.

nodes.label: Three Macro Opportunity Waves
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Macro Opportunity Waves** — A sequence of three platform-level macro opportunities — Internet, Web 2.0 (social), and AI — each spawning sub-layer micro opportunities (e.g., Google Search, Facebook Ads, TikTok Shop) with outsized early-mover returns before market stabilization.

nodes.label: Blended ROI Channel Evaluation
nodes.description: **Framework: Blended ROI Channel Evaluation** — Evaluating marketing channels by blended return rather than transaction-proximity ROI: a channel ranks high when it captures new attention AND nurtures existing audience, not merely when it sits closest to purchase.

nodes.label: Shorts as Ads to Longs
nodes.description: **Framework: Shorts as Ads to Longs** — Short-form content functions as top-of-funnel advertising whose goal is to drive audiences into longer-form content with greater total time-on-brand, not to serve as the primary engagement vehicle.

nodes.label: Supply-First Growth Sequence
nodes.description: **Framework: Supply-First Growth Sequence** — A four-to-five step prioritization sequence for operationally constrained service businesses: (1) fix supply constraint via offshoring for 2-3x delivery leverage, (2) add data architecture layer, (3) add AI layer on top of data, (4) re-open sales once new capacity is proven, (5) use existing marketing assets to grow demand.

nodes.label: Reverse-Engineer Your Enjoyment
nodes.description: **Framework: Reverse-Engineer Your Enjoyment** — A two-step creator sustainability framework: (1) identify which content formats you genuinely enjoy making, (2) capture yourself doing activities you already enjoy — then build your publishing schedule around that intersection rather than around algorithmic or audience expectations.

nodes.label: One True Lever Test
nodes.description: **Framework: One True Lever Test** — A focus-finding exercise: ask which single thing, if true in one year, would 10x the company and make all other goals follow automatically.

nodes.label: Elephant and Rider Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Elephant and Rider Framework** — Jonathan Haidt's metaphor adopted by Rory Sutherland: the elephant is System 1 (automatic, instinctive, wordless) and the rider is System 2 (conscious, rational, verbal); the rider thinks he controls the elephant but mostly post-rationalizes what the elephant already decided.

nodes.label: Acquisition Value vs Transaction Utility
nodes.description: **Framework: Acquisition Value vs Transaction Utility** — Richard Thaler's two-component purchase model: acquisition value is the objective benefit from owning or consuming the product; transaction utility is the emotional quality of the purchase act itself (fair deal vs. rip-off feeling), which can independently drive or block purchase independent of product quality.

nodes.label: Harvesting vs Hunting Optimum
nodes.description: **Framework: Harvesting vs Hunting Optimum** — An organisation (like a bee colony) needs an optimal mix of harvesting (efficient exploitation of known opportunities, ~80%) and hunting (exploratory, higher-failure-rate search for new opportunities, ~20%); 100% harvesting leads to starvation when conditions change, because rogue explorers are the adaptive mechanism.

nodes.label: Dynamic Packaging
nodes.description: **Framework: Dynamic Packaging** — A product structure that combines the flexibility of self-assembled travel booking with the legal protection of a package holiday, allowing customers to choose components (e.g. Ryanair flights + TUI hotel) within a single booking flow that confers package-holiday consumer rights.

nodes.label: Cross-Category Analysis
nodes.description: **Framework: Cross-Category Analysis** — An agency technique in which the practitioner deliberately ignores the client's own category and asks how a company from a completely different sector (e.g. Disney, airlines) would solve the same problem, surfacing insights that category-insider operators are blind to.

nodes.label: The Belgian Problem
nodes.description: **Framework: The Belgian Problem** — When marketing succeeds, observers cease to call it marketing; they attribute success to product quality, invention, or inherent advantage, making marketing's role invisible even when it was decisive.

nodes.label: Exploit vs. Explore Bee Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Exploit vs. Explore Bee Model** — Optimal resource-collection systems allocate roughly 20% of agents to random exploration (finding new sources) and 80% to exploitation (harvesting known sources); 100% exploitation traps the system in a local maximum when the known source dries up.

nodes.label: Behaviour Menu for Sustainable Change
nodes.description: **Framework: Behaviour Menu for Sustainable Change** — A menu of ~20 ranked environmental actions (small/medium/large) from which individuals choose a personal selection each year, allowing participation calibrated to personal circumstance rather than universal mandates.

nodes.label: Database-First Reactivation Sequence
nodes.plugin: Fast Cash Plays via Underutilized Assets
nodes.description: **Framework: Database-First Reactivation Sequence** — Before running any paid ads, re-engage existing lead databases and active members for reviews and referrals; use those results to build trust and organically improve ad performance before investing in cold marketing.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Fast Cash Plays via Underutilized Assets
nodes.topic: Fast Cash Plays via Underutilized Assets

nodes.label: Five-Point AI Agency Pitch Structure
nodes.description: **Framework: Five-Point AI Agency Pitch Structure** — A five-part done-for-you offer pitched sequentially: (1) database reactivation via AI, (2) review and referral automation for members, (3) targeted paid ad marketing with landing pages, (4) AI-powered lead nurture and follow-up, (5) inbound call tracking and AI answering to capture missed organic prospects.

nodes.label: Clarity-First Sales Positioning
nodes.description: **Framework: Clarity-First Sales Positioning** — Pitch only one or two simple, clear outcomes on the first call to minimize decision complexity; upsell additional services only after delivering initial results and building trust, because clarity drives faster purchase decisions.

nodes.label: Drop Low or Go High Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Drop Low or Go High Framework** — For client-acquisition agencies serving SMBs, the only viable business models are ultra-cheap high-automation or high-touch premium; the mid-market is a dead zone where margin compresses to zero.

nodes.label: Supply-First Scaling Sequence
nodes.description: **Framework: Supply-First Scaling Sequence** — When supply (capacity) is the binding constraint, the operational fix order is: (1) fix pricing/packaging to free cash flow, (2) deploy cash into paid ads with attribution, (3) invest freed margin into content/thought leadership.

nodes.label: Talent Funnel as Parallel Demand Funnel
nodes.description: **Framework: Talent Funnel as Parallel Demand Funnel** — A sales organization must build a mirror talent-acquisition funnel (applicant generation, nurture, interviewing, onboarding, retention/ascension) that receives the same budget discipline as the customer demand funnel.

nodes.label: SPCL Influence Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: SPCL Influence Framework** — Four independent but combinable components of influence: Status (control of reinforcers), Power (say-do correspondence), Credibility (third-party proof), and Likeness (similarity to audience).

nodes.label: Management Diamond
nodes.plugin: The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action
nodes.description: **Framework: Management Diamond** — A five-cause diagnostic for why an employee (or entrepreneur) is not executing a task: they did not know the task was required, did not know how to do it, did not know the deadline, had a blocking constraint, or did not want to do it — in that order of actual frequency.
nodes.parent_id: concept:The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action
nodes.topic: The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action

nodes.label: Declarative vs. Procedural Content Split
nodes.description: **Framework: Declarative vs. Procedural Content Split** — Free content teaches declarative knowledge (about how something works — what you use to sell); paid products deliver procedural knowledge (how to execute — what you sell). Mixing them causes either free riders or stalled purchases.

nodes.label: Choke Point Pre-Mortem
nodes.description: **Framework: Choke Point Pre-Mortem** — Before a high-stakes live event, enumerate every discrete failure mode in priority order and build a pre-assigned fallback for each one before the event begins.

nodes.label: $100M Series Stacking Architecture
nodes.description: **Framework: $100M Series Stacking Architecture** — A three-book product series structured so each book layers one additional skill on top of the previous (Offer -> Leads -> Money Models), written originally as one work and intentionally parsed into sequential volumes.

nodes.label: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem Definition
nodes.description: **Framework: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem Definition** — A three-question diagnostic sequence for validating any problem statement: What does it mean? How do you know? Why do I care? Forces specificity before prescribing solutions.

nodes.label: Good Friction vs Bad Friction
nodes.description: **Framework: Good Friction vs Bad Friction** — A qualification framework distinguishing friction that removes bad-fit leads and improves sales efficiency (good friction) from friction that blocks all leads indiscriminately (bad friction). Adding good friction increases ROAS and sales efficiency simultaneously.

nodes.label: Checklist-Driven Sales Ops
nodes.description: **Framework: Checklist-Driven Sales Ops** — A complete list of sales operations requirements (scripting, daily training, cultural enforcement, manager accountability) where executing the full checklist produces consistent results and any gap identifies the leader as the constraint.

nodes.label: Group-Audition Hiring Funnel
nodes.description: **Framework: Group-Audition Hiring Funnel** — A four-stage sales-rep hiring process: send script before interview, request a 60-second video audition, invite finalists to a group drill call for coachability scoring, then make job offers only to those who pass all stages.

nodes.label: Distribution Node Acquisition Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Distribution Node Acquisition Model** — Instead of tracking end-customer acquisition, count the number of distribution partners (agencies, producers) onboarded per month, treating each as a recurring referral node whose compounding output replaces the episodic churn of direct customer sales.

nodes.label: Two-Sided Education Monetization
nodes.description: **Framework: Two-Sided Education Monetization** — For certification test-prep businesses, monetize both sides of the supply-demand curve: charge students for test prep and charge universities/employers for career placement, so the same student cohort generates two revenue streams.

nodes.label: Brand Pairing Flywheel
nodes.description: **Framework: Brand Pairing Flywheel** — A four-step loop: start with a brand that means nothing, pair it deliberately with people or experiences ideal customers like, the brand inherits that meaning, customers buy to associate themselves with that meaning.

nodes.label: Advertising vs. Branding Distinction
nodes.description: **Framework: Advertising vs. Branding Distinction** — Advertising is letting people know about your product (reach/awareness); branding is the pairing and meaning that occurs as a result of that exposure. Good advertising can produce bad branding if the pairing is disliked by the target audience.

nodes.label: Galapagos Islands Loyalty Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Galapagos Islands Loyalty Framework** — A loyalty program treated as a behavioral observation environment: combining longitudinal individual-level data with a psychologist's mindset to surface anomalies, paradoxes, and small-effect insights that reveal how humans actually decide, as distinct from how economists assume they decide.

nodes.label: Explore-Exploit Trade-off (Bee Waggle Dance Model)
nodes.description: **Framework: Explore-Exploit Trade-off (Bee Waggle Dance Model)** — A resource-allocation framework in which roughly 20% of effort is devoted to random exploration of unknown opportunities (ignoring the waggle dance) and 80% exploits known reliable sources; pure exploitation produces local-maximum traps and eventual extinction.

nodes.label: SCARF Model (David Rock)
nodes.description: **Framework: SCARF Model (David Rock)** — Five dimensions humans deeply care about that economic data never captures: Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, Fairness; marketing and loyalty programs that address these create engagement that price discounts cannot replicate.

nodes.label: Consumable Input Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Consumable Input Framework** — A community offer has two separable components: (1) a one-time method/knowledge transfer and (2) recurring consumable inputs that the community must refresh each period. Retention and recurring revenue attach to the consumable layer, not to the knowledge layer.

nodes.label: Five Business Advantages Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Five Business Advantages Framework** — A five-factor scoring system (Sticky, Expensive, Expanding, Air/Low-OpEx, Unique) for evaluating and ranking the quality of a business opportunity vehicle; having even one advantage makes a business better than peers.

nodes.label: Roles-to-Workflows Shift
nodes.description: **Framework: Roles-to-Workflows Shift** — Replace role-based hiring decisions (I need an editor) with workflow-based decomposition (I need an agent for task X, an agent for task Y) by mapping every business action at its most granular level until no further reduction is possible.

nodes.label: Linear Business Workflow Map
nodes.description: **Framework: Linear Business Workflow Map** — A single continuous workflow diagram that traces every action in the business from first input (idea, inbound lead) to final output (posted content, closed deal); if you cannot draw it, the business lacks operational clarity.

nodes.label: Physics-as-Upper-Bound Standard
nodes.description: **Framework: Physics-as-Upper-Bound Standard** — Treat physical laws as the only legitimate ceiling on what a business can achieve; all other limitations are industry conventions that a sufficiently determined actor can override.

nodes.label: Attack-Vector Multiplicity Standard
nodes.description: **Framework: Attack-Vector Multiplicity Standard** — Measure the quality of someone's standards by how many distinct approaches they deploy toward a single goal before declaring it impossible; breadth of attack vectors proxies the height of standards.

nodes.label: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem-Solving Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem-Solving Framework** — A three-question sequence for breaking down any problem: (1) What does this mean? (logic/definition), (2) How do we know? (evidence), (3) Why does it matter? (utility). Applied before any claim or diagnosis is accepted.

nodes.label: Any-Answer-Except-Call-Me Operator Test
nodes.description: **Framework: Any-Answer-Except-Call-Me Operator Test** — A role-play interview used to verify a GM candidate can handle operational crises (upset customer, facility emergency) without escalating to the owner; any response except calling the owner is the right answer.

nodes.label: Sell Warm Like Cold
nodes.plugin: Warm vs. Cold Sales Process Mismatch
nodes.description: **Framework: Sell Warm Like Cold** — Apply the full cold-prospect qualification and credentialing process to every sale regardless of relationship warmth; warm prospects receive the same structured pitch as cold ones.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Warm vs. Cold Sales Process Mismatch
nodes.topic: Warm vs. Cold Sales Process Mismatch

nodes.label: Three-Option Objection Routing
nodes.description: **Framework: Three-Option Objection Routing** — When a service objection blocks a client segment, route through three options in order: (1) sell through the objection, (2) redesign delivery to remove the objection, (3) restrict the target audience to those who lack the objection.

nodes.label: Fix-Then-Scale Sequencing
nodes.description: **Framework: Fix-Then-Scale Sequencing** — Optimize unit economics and margins in existing locations before opening new ones; expansion funded by proven profitability, not ambition.

nodes.label: Sales Motion to Membership to Talent Ladder
nodes.description: **Framework: Sales Motion to Membership to Talent Ladder** — Three-stage repair sequence for stalled multi-location service businesses: (1) fix sales motion, (2) install membership model to maximize revenue per technician, (3) raise pay and build career paths to retain talent — in that order.

nodes.label: Affiliate Launch and Integration
nodes.description: **Framework: Affiliate Launch and Integration** — Two-stage affiliate activation: Launch (get 10 referrals fast to create an internal case study) followed by Integration (embed the provider into the affiliate's standard onboarding so 100% of new clients flow through, not just whoever the affiliate chooses to refer).

nodes.label: Behavioral Definition of Learning
nodes.description: **Framework: Behavioral Definition of Learning** — Learning is operationally defined as same condition producing new behavior; if condition is held constant and behavior does not change, no learning has occurred regardless of content consumed.

nodes.label: Deprivation-Reference-Point Model of Motivation
nodes.description: **Framework: Deprivation-Reference-Point Model of Motivation** — Motivation equals the inverse of perceived deprivation; for intangible constructs like money, deprivation is measured relative to a reference group, not absolute scarcity.

nodes.label: Replicate Before Iterate
nodes.description: **Framework: Replicate Before Iterate** — A two-phase learning discipline: in phase one, follow instructions exactly and replicate the teacher's results without modification; in phase two, only after replication is confirmed, apply accumulated knowledge to diverge and derive personal improvements.

nodes.label: Pareto Wealth Distribution Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Pareto Wealth Distribution Model** — Alex Hormozi maps U.S. household net worth as $100 across 100 percentiles to show that 1% of the population holds $32, more than the bottom 90% combined, and uses this to guide customer targeting decisions.

nodes.label: Four-Tier Pricing Ladder
nodes.plugin: Pareto Pricing: Four-Tier Structure at 5–10x Gaps
nodes.description: **Framework: Four-Tier Pricing Ladder** — A pricing architecture with four tiers separated by 5–10x price jumps, expecting approximately 20% of customers to ascend each tier; each tier is designed to roughly double total revenue.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Pareto Pricing: Four-Tier Structure at 5–10x Gaps
nodes.topic: Pareto Pricing: Four-Tier Structure at 5–10x Gaps

nodes.label: Close Rate as Pricing Diagnostic
nodes.plugin: Close Rate as Pricing Calibration Signal
nodes.description: **Framework: Close Rate as Pricing Diagnostic** — Alex Hormozi's rubric for diagnosing pricing power from observed close rates: 60–80% indicates 3–4x underpricing, 50–60% indicates 1.5–2x, 40–50% indicates 1.25–1.5x, 30–40% is correctly priced, below 30% indicates a sales or qualification problem.
nodes.parent_id: concept:Close Rate as Pricing Calibration Signal
nodes.topic: Close Rate as Pricing Calibration Signal

nodes.label: Prospect-Driven Sales Process
nodes.description: **Framework: Prospect-Driven Sales Process** — A scalable sales structure in which the salesperson asks questions in a prescribed order to lead the prospect to their own purchase decision, rather than demonstrating expertise or authority.

nodes.label: Top-Down Business Launch Sequence
nodes.description: **Framework: Top-Down Business Launch Sequence** — Start with a high-price, limited-volume premium offering; use early profits and brand equity to fund progressively higher-volume, lower-price tiers; never enter from the bottom and attempt to move up.

nodes.label: ROAS Doom Loop
nodes.description: **Framework: ROAS Doom Loop** — A self-reinforcing trap in which DTC brands keep increasing ad spend to reach less profitable audiences, compressing margins further until revenue equals spend with no net gain.

nodes.label: CRO as Steroids
nodes.description: **Framework: CRO as Steroids** — Conversion-rate optimization yields a one-time lift (sometimes 2-3x) but establishes a new baseline rather than resolving the structural front-end traffic and brand deficit.

nodes.label: SPCL Influence Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: SPCL Influence Framework** — A four-component model for building content-based influence: Status (controlling scarce reinforcers), Power (say-do correspondence that produces positive outcomes), Credibility (observable third-party evidence), and Likeness (shared values, aesthetics, or demographic similarity). Components stack multiplicatively — each one independently creates influence, all four together create maximal compliance likelihood.

nodes.label: Product-as-Marketing Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Product-as-Marketing Framework** — In businesses where discovery is dominated by word-of-mouth and reviews (e.g., restaurants), product quality and experience ARE the marketing spend; premium investment in ingredients, service, and environment replaces advertising as the primary acquisition lever.

nodes.label: Grand Opening Playbook
nodes.description: **Framework: Grand Opening Playbook** — A staged launch protocol for new physical locations: overstaff, run multi-channel ads, and deploy promotional giveaways (or exclusive invite-only events for premium concepts) to generate sufficient initial word-of-mouth so the location reaches full capacity within six months organically.

nodes.label: Sales Ops Checklist
nodes.description: **Framework: Sales Ops Checklist** — A complete list of sales operations requirements — daily training, script memorization, script enforcement, and manager accountability — that together produce consistent close rates; missing any items and you do not get the outcome.

nodes.label: Group Screening Funnel for Sales Reps
nodes.description: **Framework: Group Screening Funnel for Sales Reps** — A three-stage hiring filter for sales reps: (1) send script before interview and request 60-second video recitation; (2) invite passing candidates to a group coaching call and evaluate coachability under live feedback; (3) extend job offers only to those who demonstrated preparation and coachability.

nodes.label: Three Traits of Hyper-Successful People
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Traits of Hyper-Successful People** — Hyper-successful people share three co-occurring traits: (1) grandiose vision with an inflated superiority complex, (2) crippling insecurity where they feel they will never be good enough, and (3) strong impulse control enabling sustained focus over extended periods.

nodes.label: Input-Output Equation
nodes.description: **Framework: Input-Output Equation** — A two-step framework: (1) define the specific input action that produces your desired output, then (2) multiply that input by 10x or 100x to reach the corresponding outcome at scale.

nodes.label: Three Levels of Leverage Stack
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Levels of Leverage Stack** — A three-tier model illustrating increasing leverage on a single input action: Level 1 = do the action yourself, Level 2 = hire someone to do the action for you (same output, no founder effort), Level 3 = hire a recruiter who brings a new doer each week so the input compounds indefinitely without additional founder effort.

nodes.label: Sequential Control Relinquishment
nodes.description: **Framework: Sequential Control Relinquishment** — A staged model in which founders must surrender control of business functions in a fixed sequence to unlock leverage at each stage: delivery/production, admin, sales, marketing, management, leadership, financing, and finally the need to be needed by the business.

nodes.label: Paid Ads More Sequence
nodes.description: **Framework: Paid Ads More Sequence** — Three-step risk-ordered sequence for scaling paid advertising: (1) make more creative, (2) spend more money, (3) expand to more platforms — each step unlocks the next.

nodes.label: Count in Hundreds Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Count in Hundreds Framework** — Measure depth of mastery by counting effort in units of hundreds of hours rather than hours; the shift in unit of measurement forces a qualitatively different level of engagement with the subject.

nodes.label: Done When Nothing More Can Be Improved
nodes.description: **Framework: Done When Nothing More Can Be Improved** — Work is declared complete not when time runs out but when the producer cannot identify any further change that would make the output better; this redefines done from time-based to quality-based.

nodes.label: Work Works on You More Than You Work on It
nodes.description: **Framework: Work Works on You More Than You Work on It** — The output of sustained effort is not only the external result but the transformation of the person doing the work; the worker becomes the primary asset produced.

nodes.label: Mountain Climbing Capacity Metaphor
nodes.description: **Framework: Mountain Climbing Capacity Metaphor** — Smaller mountains must be climbed before larger ones; each climb builds the capacity and belief needed to attempt the next, higher mountain. Maps to: small wins -> compounding capability -> readiness for bigger challenges.

nodes.label: Inverse PTSD Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Inverse PTSD Framework** — Each survived hardship serves as exposure therapy, raising the experiential floor of what you know you can handle; subsequent challenges feel survivable because prior evidence confirms you did not die.

nodes.label: Two-Vector Learning Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Two-Vector Learning Framework** — Intelligence can be improved on two independent axes: reducing the number of iterations required to change behavior, OR compressing the time between iterations so the total elapsed time to behavior change is lower.

nodes.label: Skill as Chained Behaviors
nodes.description: **Framework: Skill as Chained Behaviors** — A skill is a sequence of individually learned same-condition/new-behavior pairs chained together; each link in the chain is a discrete learning event.

nodes.label: Consumable Media Framework
nodes.description: **Framework: Consumable Media Framework** — A three-part model for membership businesses: sell the system (education) once up front, then supply the monthly consumable inputs that make the system work, reducing churn by ensuring members need the product every single month.

nodes.label: Three Levels of Accountability
nodes.description: **Framework: Three Levels of Accountability** — Peer-to-peer (shoulder-to-shoulder with someone at the same stage), alumni (one step ahead, cheerleading), and expert (has solved the problem hundreds of times) accountability layers sold as a retention and value-delivery system inside membership offers.

nodes.label: Ink-Printer Revenue Model
nodes.description: **Framework: Ink-Printer Revenue Model** — Sell the machine (system, education) once; sell the ink (consumable inputs) repeatedly every month. The initial one-time sale enables a recurring revenue stream from the supplies the machine requires.

nodes.label: Reframing Through Narrative
nodes.description: **Framework: Reframing Through Narrative** — Changing the linguistic and contextual frame applied to a situation alters human emotional and perceptual response to that situation, without changing the objective facts.
